stories.title: Warriors' Jimmy Butler says he won't be 'a bum-a** player' upon return from torn ACL
stories.summary: Prior to tearing his ACL in January, Butler was putting up his best numbers of the past four seasons.
stories.detailText: Did Jimmy Butler let the Golden State Warriors down when he tore his right ACL in January ? That seems like an awfully harsh assessment, but the veteran scorer feels that his injury prevented him from fulfiling expectations, something he's eager to amend. Going into his 16th NBA season, Butler is determined to justify the faith the Warriors showed in trading for him during the 2024-25 season . Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Without Butler, Golden State went 12-26 for the remainder of the season and barely qualified for the posteason as the No. 10 seed in the Western Conference. That got the Warriors into the Play-In Tournament , where they defeated the Los Angeles Clippers before getting eliminated by the Phoenix Suns in a blowout loss . "I really felt like I let Steph [Curry] down," Butler told ESPN's Anthony Slater . "I let Draymond [Green] down. I let Steve [Kerr] down. Because they took a chance." "If you don't know me and you haven't been around me, you don't know what I'm about because of the things that you may read and hear," he continued. At the time he was injured, Butler was having a resurgent season, averaging 20 points, 5.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists per game. He was also shooting 38% on 85 3-point attempts. Butler, 37, didn't say when exactly he would return while speaking with Slater during training camp. But he and the Warriors have a target date in mind. "I know," Butler told Slater. "We know. Y'all just find out whenever y'all find out." Jimmy Butler on how he’s feeling and what’s a realistic target date for his return: “I’m feeling great. Surgery went well. We’ve been obviously doing this rehab thing, going through that process. But all in all, I’m back moving on the floor, some running, jogging, doing all of… pic.twitter.com/IMbHX8iOyv — aly ✶ (@jinthirty) October 16, 2026 Butler's encouraging recovery points him to taking the court again in January or February. When he returns for his 16th NBA season, Butler is determined to demonstrate that he can still be an impact player who can help the Warriors make one last playoff run. He wants one more chance at the NBA championship that's alluded him during his career. "That's why I say y'all motherf***ers going to be real shocked if y'all think I'm going to come back and be some bum-a** player," he said. Butler's bravado was missed by the Warriors after he was sidelined, according to Kerr. "He's such an alpha," Kerr said . "Everyone feels so confident when he's on the floor. There's just a sense of swagger that you have when Jimmy's on your team. So, it felt like we lost that instantly." The Warriors tip off the 2026-27 season Wednesday at the Los Angeles Lakers.

stories.title: Rockets Amen Thompson named best perimeter defender by NBA GMs
stories.summary: High praise for Amen from GMs.
stories.detailText: Every year, the NBA General Managers take a survey voting on certain topics such as best defender, player most likely to have a breakout season, best assistant coach, etc. What keeps this survey honest is that general managers are not allowed to vote for any of their players or staff. If you want to read the survey for yourself, you can do so here . This year, one particular Rocket was mentioned repeatedly in the survey, and that is Wing Amen Thompson, who scored second for most likely to break out, scored fourth for what player can move the ball fastest, and second for most adaptable defender (behind only Wembanyama), amongst other awards. Amen Thompson scored first in two categories, those being best perimeter defender and most athletic. For best perimeter defender, Thompson garnered 30% of the vote, surpassing both his twin brother Ausar Thompson and Alex Caruso, who both received 17%. In the athletic category, he was even more dominant, winning 63% of the vote, far more than Anthony Edwards, who came in second with 20%. Anyone who has followed Thompson during the previous two seasons with the Rockets shouldn’t be surprised by either outcome, in my opinion. The fact that NBA executives are showing him this much respect before he even starts his fourth NBA season is even more impressive. Amen Thompson is already regarded as one of the NBA’s best defenders. Even while he has the bulk to compete with larger wings at 6’7”, what really stands out is his ability to stay ahead of smaller, speedier guards. When an attacking player steps on him, few players have the length and speed to recover and still make a move. I also love how defensively aggressive Thompson is without constantly changing positions. He doesn’t need to risk steals to make a mark because his length, speed, and ability to contest shots already make opponents uncomfortable. It is a big honor for Rockets coach Ime Udoka to be able to pair Thompson with the top perimeter scorer on the opposing team and trust him to carry it out. In my opinion, Thompson has a good chance of winning Defensive Player of the Year at some point in his career. When you’re up against exceptional rim protectors like Victor Wembanyama, it’s clearly hard for perimeter defenders to win this honor, but I can see Thompson maybe winning the award if Wembanyama has a down year, or if there is voter fatigue. Outside of Amen Thompson, head coach Ime Udoka tied for second place in the GM survey when asked which head coach has the strongest defensive tactics. On the question of which assistant coach is the best in the league, Royal Ivey was tied for third. When asked which player General Managers would most like to try with the game on the line, All-Star forward Kevin Durant, who was selected to the second team of the NBA the previous season, came in fifth. In the “best small forward” poll, he also garnered votes. What do you think about the GM survey? Do you agree with the results, or disagree? stories.title: Bucks make way for Brewers’ World Series return with schedule change
stories.summary: The Bucks moved its home opener against the Bulls to avoid a conflict with the Brewers’ long-awaited World Series return.
stories.detailText: The Milwaukee Brewers are making history , and the city’s NBA franchise doesn’t want to impede that in any way. The Bucks and NBA announced Friday, Oct. 16 that the team’s home opener against the Chicago Bulls has been moved up four hours to prevent a scheduling conflict with Game 1 of the World Series on Friday, Oct. 23, which will take place in Milwaukee and mark the club’s first trip to the Fall Classic in more than four decades . "The Brewers' return to the World Series for the first time in 44 years is a special moment for Milwaukee and sports fans across Wisconsin," the Bucks said Friday in a statement . "Congratulations to the Brewers and the entire organization on this tremendous achievement, and we’ll be cheering them on as they begin their World Series run. The Bucks are proud to move our home opener to 3 p.m. (CT), in recognition of this historic occasion and thank the NBA for making this schedule change possible." The Brewers clinched the National League pennant Thursday, Oct. 15 with their sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers. They will face the winner of the American League Championship Series between the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays. Cleveland leads that series, 2-1, and Game 4 is scheduled for Friday night . It’s unconventional for an NBA team to move its home opener like this, but the Brewers will be hosting Game 1 at American Family Field. The Brewers had the best record in baseball and are one of five MLB teams to have never won a World Series. This will be only their second trip to the Fall Classic. The Bucks, meanwhile, are projected to be one of the worst teams in the NBA as they are undergoing a rebuild following their offseason blockbuster trade that sent Giannis Antetokounmpo, the franchise’s all-time leader in points (21,531), rebounds (8,882), assists (4,484), blocks (1,088) and triple-doubles (56) to the Miami Heat. stories.title: Knicks reportedly exploring Pacome Dadiet, Tyler Kolek trades so they can keep Bruce Brown
stories.summary: The Knicks staff likes the veteran guard Brown, but just keeping him pushes them over the second apron.
stories.detailText: While the Knicks brought in a number of veterans on non-guaranteed contracts to compete for a roster spot in training camp, James Wiseman was always the frontrunner. New York needs depth at center behind Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond, and Wiseman fits that role well. When the Knicks cut Drew Eubanks, Tony Bradley and Ochai Agbaji on Thursday, it cleared the way for Wiseman to make the roster. However, the Knicks also like what guard Bruce Brown brings to the table and are now looking for trades to trade either Pacome Dadiet or Tyler Kolek over the weekend to free up the money to keep Brown, according to reports from Stefan Bondy at the New York Post and Ian Begley of SNY.tv . The Knicks have the open roster spots to just bring in Wiseman and Brown as the 14th and 15th men, but doing so would push the team into the second apron, a line owner James Dolan has said the team will not cross. That leaves the Knicks looking for trade options. The Knicks have been looking for a Dadiet trade for a while, but haven't found a deal that works. Kolek was part of the Knicks rotation much of last season, playing in 62 games and averaging 4.4 points in nearly 12 minutes per game. However, when the Knicks acquired Jose Alvarado, Kolek fell out of the rotation, and he has struggled this preseason with his shot (33.3% from 3-point range and 40% overall). Kolek likely has more value around the league and is making $2.3 million this season. The challenge for the Knicks is that they aren't the only team looking to make salary-dump trades before next Monday's cut-down deadline. It is possible the Knicks attach one of their future second-round picks to facilitate a trade, Begley reports. Also, teams are "studying" the Knicks' contract situation with Karl-Anthony Towns, ESPN’s Brian Windhorst reports . "Studying" is the new term for "monitoring" a situation. If Towns declines his player option for next season (he is expected to, the deadline is Monday) and the sides don't reach a deal, then Towns will be a free agent next summer, and of course there are teams interested. The Warriors, Hawks and Clippers are expected to have max cap space. While the Knicks hit the pause button on extension talks with Towns, the expectation is that the sides will reach a deal before Towns hits the open market.

stories.title: Buss siblings' filing challenges Jeanie's petition to oust them as trustees
stories.summary: The legal jostling between five of the Buss siblings against their sister, Lakers acting governor Jeanie Buss, continued with an additional filing submitted to the Los Angeles Superior Court.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES -- The legal jostling between five of the Buss siblings against their sister, Lakers acting governor Jeanie Buss, continued Friday with an additional filing submitted to the Los Angeles Superior Court. The 29-page document, reviewed by ESPN, was filed on behalf of Joey and Janie Buss in opposition to their sister and her previous petition seeking to remove them as co-trustees and void the siblings' 5-1 vote to sell the family's remaining stake in the team. "This dispute turns on (1) who had the authority to decide whether the Trust would continue, (2) what event would terminate it, and (3) what the Trustee Respondents were required to do once that event occurred," Friday's filing says. "The Trust's text unambiguously answers each question." The new filing not only argues Joey and Janie's right to hold the vote to sell and highlights language in the trust that states a sale requires a two-thirds majority by the siblings, which they exceeded, but it also challenges the breadth of Jeanie's rights as a co-trustee and acting governor. The filing follows a 36-page opposition submitted to the court Oct. 7 by all five siblings -- Jimmy, Johnny and Jesse included -- that argued their right to terminate the family trust and sell their remaining 17.82% of the team to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger's ownership group after the pair agreed to purchase the Lakers from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation. Both filings come in response to Jeanie, through her lawyer Adam Streisand, submitting a 97-page petition to the court in August aimed to block the sale of the family's stake in the team to Kushner and Iger, who, sources told ESPN, are expected to take control of the franchise following an NBA board of governors vote in November. Friday's filing contends that a 2017 court decision that instructed the trustees to take "whatever actions are reasonably available" to have Jeanie appointed as the controlling owner while the family trust holds Lakers stock became moot once a vote was held to terminate the trust to facilitate a sale. "It does not require the Trust to remain in existence for Jeanie's lifetime ... or require the Trust to maintain any minimum ownership percentage," the filing states. The NBA requires a controlling owner to maintain a 15% stake in a team to operate in that position, though Friday's filing states that the 15% figure is not included anywhere in the original trust or in the 2017 order. The new filing also contends that while the family trust barred any sale of Lakers stock during Dr. Jerry Buss' lifetime without his consent, it contains no comparable restriction connected to Jeanie. Furthermore, Friday's filing argues that a sale to Kushner and Iger will maximize value of the trust's 185.59 shares of the Lakers for all the beneficiaries, including Jeanie. The filing covers two contractual sale rights the trust secured when the Walter transaction was finalized in 2025: a go-along right (commonly referred to as a tagalong provision) and a separate put right. The put right granted by Walter would allow the siblings to sell their remaining shares at the same $10 billion valuation at which he bought the majority stake of the franchise, at discretion. The tagalong provision, agreed to at the same time, would allow the siblings to sell their shares to a new ownership group at the franchise's new valuation -- in this case $12.5 billion -- if Walter ever sold his interest in the team. The filing argues that Joey and Janie enacting a vote to sell via the tagalong provision represented the more favorable economic opportunity for the trust and all six beneficiaries. Additionally, the new filing argues that Jeanie's petition, which held her siblings in contempt, lacks merit and asks the court to dismiss the claim. The siblings exercised voting rights expressly granted to them as beneficiaries, which the filing argues cannot constitute contempt or aiding and abetting a fiduciary breach. "There is deep irony in [Jeanie] alleging that it is [Joey and Janie] who are putting their self-interests first," the filing says. "The entire petition [originally filed by Jeanie] is predicated on the notion that rights expressly granted to the beneficiaries by [the trust] should be subjugated to [Jeanie's] personal interest in remaining controlling owner. [Jeanie's] hypocrisy should not go unnoticed."

stories.title: Spanish club contesting NBA eligibility of Thunder rookie Aday Mara over contract dispute
stories.summary: The Thunder insist that the center is eligible to play for them despite his former club in Spain saying that it continues to hold his rights.
stories.detailText: The Oklahoma City Thunder insisted Friday that rookie center Aday Mara is eligible to play for the team, despite claims raised by the lottery pick's former club in Spain that it would need to release him from the terms of the contract he signed with them as a teenager for him to be able to play in the NBA. The Spanish newspaper Heraldo de Aragón reported Friday that Liga ACB club Casademont Zaragoza claims it holds the playing rights to Mara — a 7-foot-3 center whom the Thunder selected out of Michigan with the No. 12 overall pick in June's NBA Draft — through 2027, and plans to block his ability to play for another club "until a financial settlement regarding his departure is reached," according to Johnny Askounis of Eurohoops . Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season "Basket Zaragoza wishes Aday Mara the best of luck in his new sporting endeavors and remains committed to developing players in its youth academy," Zaragoza wrote in a statement . "At the same time, as an organization, the Club has an obligation to protect its rights, ensure compliance with existing contracts, and defend the interests of Basket Zaragoza, taking all necessary legal action." The Thunder, for their part, say that Zaragoza's statement and claims have no bearing on whether or not Mara will be eligible to suit up when the Thunder open the 2026-27 NBA regular season. "Aday last played three years of NCAA college basketball and therefore, as advised by the NBA, no clearance from the Spanish team is required for him to play in the NBA," a Thunder spokesperson told Yahoo Sports. Oklahoma City Thunder rookie center Aday Mara protects the rim during a preseason game against the Atlanta Hawks. (AP/Mike Stewart) AP Photo/Mike Stewart Mara began his playing career with Zaragoza, his hometown club, making his first-team debut back in 2021 at the age of 16. When Mara came over to the U.S. in 2023, signing with UCLA as a heralded five-star recruit, Zaragoza contested his eligibility, claiming that he remained under contract with his club in Spain and thus was not free to play elsewhere. "The message that a prestigious university like this sends is that contracts between parties do not have to be fulfilled," Zaragoza general manager Jose Artigas wrote in an email to Ben Bolch of the Los Angeles Times . "I don't know what the UCLA law professors would think." The club sued Mara for breach of contract, seeking more than $600,000 to allow him to exit his deal. "We want him to fulfill the contract," Artigas wrote . "And if he wants to leave, he must pay." Mara was ultimately cleared to play for the Bruins just before the start of the 2023-24 college basketball season, and averaged 5.0 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.2 blocks in 11.5 minutes per game across two seasons in Westwood. He then transferred to Ann Arbor for the 2025-26 campaign and blossomed, making more than two-thirds of his field goal attempts and earning Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year honors as the starting center for a Wolverines squad that went 37-3 and won the national championship. The gifts Mara showcased at Michigan — the scoring touch on the interior, the shot-blocking acumen, the deft touch as a passer — combined with his 7-foot-3, 255-pound, 7-foot-6-wingspan frame to make him a lottery selection, chosen by the Thunder with the 12th pick in June's draft. The 21-year-old turned heads throughout preseason play , averaging 13.4 points, 7.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 2.4 blocks in 23.3 minutes per game and making an impact on both ends of the floor: But with Mara poised to make his NBA debut next week, Zaragoza has renewed its objections to him plying his trade for another professional organization. "FIBA regulations do not require an international transfer to play in the NCAA, which does not recognize it," Zaragoza wrote in a statement . "Therefore, when [Mara] joined UCLA (NCAA) in 2023, the club did not make his departure contingent on the granting of a transfer, but rather defended its rights in court. This does not mean that his departure terminated his contract or that he was excluded from the FIBA ​​system." As it stands, it appears Mara will be eligible to participate when Oklahoma City tip off the season against the rival San Antonio Spurs and 7-foot-5 MVP finalist Victor Wembanyama in Texas on Tuesday night.

stories.title: Spanish team challenging Thunder rookie Aday Mara's NBA eligibility
stories.summary: A Spanish basketball team is challenging Thunder rookie Aday Mara's eligibility to play in the NBA this season, saying he is still under contract with the club.
stories.detailText: Spanish club Basket Zaragoza is challenging Oklahoma City Thunder rookie lottery pick Aday Mara 's eligibility to play in the NBA this season, stating that he remains under contract with the team for the 2026-27 season, a contention disputed by the Thunder. In a statement released Friday, Basket Zaragoza said it has not received an official request from the Thunder for Mara's international transfer and would formally oppose the transfer if a request is made. "Aday last played three years of NCAA college basketball and therefore, as advised by the NBA, no clearance from the Spanish team is required for him to play in the NBA," a Thunder spokesperson said Friday. Basket Zaragoza said its position was formally communicated to FIBA, the Spanish Basketball Federation, the NBA and the Thunder after Oklahoma City selected Mara with the No. 12 pick in June's draft. Mara, a native of Zaragoza, left the club in 2023 to go to UCLA . However, FIBA regulations do not require an official international transfer for NCAA participation, and Basket Zaragoza's stance is that Mara's contract with the club was not terminated during his college tenure. After two seasons at UCLA, the 7-foot-3 Mara transferred to Michigan , where he started on last season's national championship team before entering the draft. The 21-year-old Mara had an outstanding preseason for Oklahoma City, averaging 13.4 points, 7.6 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 2.4 blocks while shooting 78.8% from the floor in 23.3 minutes per game. He is projected to be part of a deep center rotation for the Thunder, who use 7-footers Isaiah Hartenstein and Chet Holmgren in the starting lineup and bring Jaylin Williams off the bench.

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Mary Kate Ridgway/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The James Harden for Darius Garland swap was one of the more shocking trades of the past few deadlines. It was one of those deals where you assume you’re being ‘ centeled ’. Once the confusion and initial shock clear, it becomes a question of how and why the Cleveland Cavaliers , and more specifically Cavaliers President of Basketball Operations Koby Altman, made this move. However, it appears that he might not have been the primary catalyst for getting the deal done. In a recent article, Yaron Weitzman of The Ringer noted that “ the Cavs’ February trade for James Harden was the direct result of back-channel talks between Gansey, who by then was Cleveland’s no. 2 to Altman in the front office, and Harden’s agents .” This makes Gansey’s departure and his construction of the league’s newest super team with the Philadelphia 76ers sting a little more than it already did. The Cavaliers have made a lot of trades over the past half-decade, e.g., Donovan Mitchell, Max Strus, Caris LeVert, and De’Andre Hunter. Statements like Weitzman’s raise questions about how involved Gansey was in getting those deals done. It’s natural to wonder how the Cavaliers will perform in trades now that Gansey is out of the building. If the team’s track record begins to change, Altman will draw more criticism and less credit. While it seems unfair to try to figure out who was more responsible for trades, Altman has always been known as someone willing to take a swing. If that changes, questions about who was really driving those daring choices will emerge.

stories.title: Did the NBA General Manager Survey disrespect the Suns?
stories.summary: Phoenix has contenders but no nominees for most categories, with a chance to prove their case in 2026-27.
stories.detailText: PHOENIX, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 28: Head coach Jordan Ott of the Phoenix Suns poses for a portrait during NBA media day on September 28, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Annually for the past 25 years, the NBA has anonymously surveyed general managers with a range of questions (48!) focused on rating teams, front offices, coaches, and players. This provides good insight into what the league’s decision-makers really think. Results published earlier this week. For this audience of hardcore Suns fans, I will view it through the lens of what it implies for team perception and where there are opportunities to appear more prominently if this was completed again at the end of the upcoming season. Team Rankings Phoenix did not receive any top 4 votes for “Who will win the 2027 NBA Finals?”. Points are awarded based on each GM’s 1-4 rank and then aggregated. Total points are sorted to provide a conference ranking. In order: Spurs Thunder Timberwolves Nuggets Rockets Lakers Trail Blazers The Suns did not receive any top 4 votes. This team definitely has the potential to pass each of the teams ranked 3-7 if everything falls right. Front Office The team struck out on this set of questions, which included best overall moves, most improved team, biggest impact acquisition, and most underrated acquisition. If Miles Bridges plays fully up to his potential, adding defensive and playmaking chops to scoring ability and athleticism, he could make a notable difference for the Suns when compared to last year with Royce O’Neale filling that starting spot. What caught my eye: 15 players mentioned as the most underrated acquisition, and none of those were Luke Kennard. The preseason has teased the well-rounded skill set he brings to go along with sniper-level long-range shooting. Getting up 10 threes in one preseason game suggests he may do that on some level of volume. I wrote in September about how important Kennard will be in balancing long-range shooting on the left side of the court. There is a tangible likelihood he ends up being one of the 15 most underrated NBA moves, especially on that $6 million contract. Coaching The good news: Jordan Ott received votes for both “runs the best offense” and “has the best defensive schemes”. However, he did not get votes for best head coach. Similarly, Ott was absent from the categories of “best manager/motivator” and “best in-game adjustments”. In year two, these are both areas I could see improvement. Pushing the right buttons emotionally and with game tactics could bump up the Suns’ win total and catapult him into future top coach discussions. Players The majority of the survey’s questions relate to players. The game is played on the court, and it’s a player’s league! It’s completely fair that no Suns were mentioned for some categories like MVP. Here are the ones where I feel consideration should have been given and could certainly be earned: Most likely to have a breakout season: Mostly young developing players among the 19 mentioned. stories.title: NBA Preview 2026-27: Seven players most likely to be traded this season
stories.summary: Despite the best efforts of Masai Ujiri, Kyrie Irving tops the list. Anthony Davis is there, too.
stories.detailText: The NBA trade deadline is four months away. That may feel like a lifetime on the NBA calendar — teams will be more than 50 games into the season, and many franchises' fortunes will look different — but it doesn't slow the NBA rumor mill. Which players might be available is already a talking point, and those conversations are only going to get louder. Here are seven names to watch, seven players most likely to be traded before the February deadline. Kyrie Irving (Mavericks) "I think it was Kevin Durant that said it best: There's only one Kyrie walking around in the world... Kyrie, as a player, we truly believe in him. We truly believe that he can succeed on our team." Dallas Mavericks president Masai Ujiri keeps saying things like the quote above, trying to throw cold water on the idea that the Mavericks are going to trade the nine-time All-Star point guard. Ujiri and Mavericks fans — and basketball fans everywhere — want to see what Irving and his legendary handles look like next to the fast-rising Cooper Flagg. Ujiri keeps talking up Irving's fit in Dallas and how the point guard can lift this team to new heights. It's not working. League sources tell NBC Sports that a number of teams are monitoring the situation, waiting to see how Irving looks coming off missing all of last season due to a torn ACL, but those teams are interested in a trade. Those teams will be calling. The reality is the 34-year-old Irving, who can be a free agent this summer, is not on the same timeline as the 19-year-old Flagg, and ultimately the Mavericks are going to want to build out a roster closer to Flagg's timeline. Ujiri can say whatever he wants, but teams around the league believe if the right offer comes his way at the deadline, Irving will be on the move. Anthony Davis (Wizards) The Wizards drafted forward AJ Dybantsa with the No. 1 pick, locked up Trae Young with a massive overpay new four-year contract, and have the big man of the future in the promising Alex Sarr. Then there is Anthony Davis, the 33-year-old NBA champion and 10-time All-Star who remains one of the best big men in the game when healthy (but being healthy has been an issue). Washington has other concerns: Davis is not on Dybantsa's or Sarr's timeline (not that Young is), plus Davis is extension-eligible and looking for another massive payday. The Wizards have put off contract talks until later in the season. If Davis stays healthy and looks good as we approach the trade deadline, the Wizards will get calls. Quality big men, especially ones who can protect the rim, are in high demand, and the Wizards may be able to get Davis to a place where he can compete for another ring while getting themselves young players and picks that better fit the Dybantsa timeline. Domantas Sabonis (Kings) The Kings have spent more than a year trying to find a new home for Sabonis, but maybe it finally happens at this year's deadline. Although probably not. The issue isn't his production, Sabonis is an efficient double-double machine who can operate as an offensive hub at the elbow and is strong on the boards. He'll show off his value this season because he's a good big to pair with Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr., setting screens and running dribble hand-offs. Plus, Sabonis is a quality passing big. What has slowed finding a trade is Sabonis' salary: $45.4 million this season and $48.6 million next season, both years fully guaranteed. In the apron era, teams don't want to pay that for a player who is not a star. However, maybe at the deadline a team that just needs a quality big will call Sacramento and make a deal. Otherwise, expect one next summer. Michael Porter Jr. (Nets) The Brooklyn Nets are rebuilding and Michael Porter Jr. is not on that timeline. Coming off his best season, MPJ is a bucket who averaged 24.2 points and 7.1 rebounds a game, and is a career 39.8% from beyond the arc. He's a 6'10" forward who is in his prime at age 28, and on an expiring $40.1 million contract. Then there's the fact that the Nets just traded for a ball-dominant forward in Julius Randle. The Nets have what they hope is their young backcourt of the future — Mikel Brown Jr. and Egor Dëmin — and if they can trade Porter Jr. for a young player or more picks, that makes sense for a rebuilding team (that does not control its own pick this season). Max Strus (and every veteran on the Clippers) The Clippers have a lot of work to do on this roster going forward, whatever it's going to look like (they like the idea of Darius Garland and Keaton Wagler backcourt). The Clippers also could use more picks, since they just had to surrender a bunch in the Kawhi Leonard/Aspiration scandal and punishment. Not that Max Strus is going to draw a first-rounder, but once he gets healthy and if he can show he adds value — as he did for the Cavaliers in last season's playoffs — he could net the Clippers a couple of second-rounders. They'd take that. Zion Williamson (Pelicans) Free Trey Murphy. Other teams are going to call about Murphy and Herb Jones, but where are the Pelicans with Zion Williamson? Could the Pelicans trade the former No. 1 pick? The reality is New Orleans is more invested in a future with Derik Queen at the four, and we learned last season that Queen and Williamson can't play together. Maybe team president Joe Dumars tries to move Williamson, who is coming off a relatively healthy season (62 games) where he averaged 21 points and 5.7 rebounds a game. The challenge is that Zion makes $42.2 million this season and has a guaranteed $44.9 million next season, so it'll be tough to get a team to take him on. Still, the rumors will fly. Also, Dumars could just trade Trey Murphy. Daniel Gafford (Mavericks) Daniel Gafford's availability in a trade is dependent upon whether Dereck Lively can get and stay healthy. If he does, and if rookie Morez Johnson shows he can handle backup big minutes, then Gafford becomes available. We mentioned above how center is a position in demand, and teams that don't want to pay for someone like Anthony Davis will call about Gafford. The seven-year NBA veteran is a rock-solid on both ends of the court, a pick-and-roll big who averaged 9.5 points and 6.9 rebounds a game last season. He's also on a reasonable contract, making $17.3 million this season with two more guaranteed years after that at a little more than $37 million total. As the deadline approaches, expect a lot of Gafford rumors. Honorable mention: Tyler Herro and anyone else in Milwaukee not just drafted, Jarrett Allen in Cleveland (if things go sideways and the Cavs need to make a move, this is the most logical player to trade), Zach LaVine in Sacramento, Jrue Holiday in Portland, Jalen Green in Phoenix. Free Trey Murphy. Some people want to put Joel Embiid on these lists. Good luck with that. The oft-injured center is making $58.1 million this season and has two more seasons on his current deal after that, totaling $130 million. No team will take that contract unless the 76ers attach multiple first-round picks or add a quality young player. Philly won't do that. Meaning Embiid stays. Also, the Knicks aren't going to trade Karl-Anthony Towns. It's an easy, clickbait story to say other teams are monitoring the situation — of course they are, this is what other front offices are paid to do — but the Knicks aren't trading him at the deadline. The KAT future story only gets interesting if he doesn't get an extension before the deadline next June 30 (and hits the free agent market). Until then, it's all speculation.

stories.title: Buss family asks judge to dismiss Jeanie Buss' petition to block Lakers share sale
stories.summary: Janie and Joey Buss asked a judge on Friday to dismiss Jeanie Buss' claim the family trust cannot the sell Lakers shares without her consent.
stories.detailText: Lakers governor Jeanie Buss filed a lawsuit arguing her siblings cannot sell the family's Lakers ownership shares without her consent. (Kayla Bartkowski/Los Angeles Times) Lawyers for Janie and Joey Buss, two of the co-trustees of the Buss Family Trust that owns part of the Lakers, filed a response to Jeanie Buss’ petition Friday with intention to move forward with the proposed sale of the family’s remaining shares of the team. While Jeanie is trying to block her five siblings from selling the team, the new response filed in L.A. Superior Court states that Janie and Joey, the two other co-trustees of the family trust, were authorized and required to implement the vote after a majority of the living siblings opted to terminate the trust in August. The vote of five siblings to sell the shares triggered the termination clause in the trust, and the filing argues that the trust doesn’t grant trustees discretion to disregard a valid vote to terminate. The filing, which follows formal opposition filed on behalf of five Buss siblings last week that defended their right to vote to sell the team, asks the court to dismiss Jeanie’s petition or deny it in its entirety. Jeanie argued that her siblings could not terminate the family trust and sell the remaining 17.82% of the team without her approval, citing a 2017 court order that instructed trustees to “take reasonably available steps” to support Jeanie’s annual election as Lakers controlling governor. The court order, obtained after Jeanie’s older brothers Jimmy and Johnny Buss tried to oust her from the organization, installed Janie and Joey as co-trustees. Read more: Jeanie Buss' siblings file formal opposition to her attempt to block sale of Lakers But the court order did not prohibit a sale or termination of the trust, lawyers for Janie and Joey argue. While the order named “voting the trust’s shares” as a reasonable action, it did not require the trust to hold a 15% stake in the team to reach the NBA’s eligibility threshold for minority owners to serve on the league’s board of governors, the filing states. Jeanie was selected by her father, Jerry Buss , to serve as the team’s controlling governor after his death in 2013. Since the family patriarch bought the team, the Forum and the Kings for $67.5 million in 1979, the Lakers have become one of the most valuable brands in sports. Mark Walter , who purchased controlling ownership from the Buss siblings in 2025, sold his shares to venture capitalist Joshua Kushner and former Disney chief executive Bob Iger 14 months later at a record $12.5 billion valuation. Read more: Inside the Buss family's long, painful history of sibling rivalries running the Lakers Using a tag-along provision secured during the sale to Walter, the five Buss siblings hope to maximize value for all six beneficiaries, including Jeanie, the new filing reports. Selling the 17.82% stake in the team would be worth about $2.2 billion. A hearing is scheduled for Dec. 8. The Lakers open the regular season on Oct. 21 against the Golden State Warriors at Crypto.com Arena. Jeanie was seen at the Lakers’ home preseason opener on Oct. 8, sitting courtside on the baseline. stories.title: Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla: Getting BJJ blue belt felt the same as winning NBA title
stories.summary: The Boston Celtics head coach says receiving his jiu-jitsu blue belt felt the same as winning the NBA title.
stories.detailText: Boston Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla holding the NBA title in 2024. | Photo by Elsa/Getty Images Boston Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla has all but booked a spot in the Hall of Fame, despite still being the youngest active NBA head coach. In just four years in his role, he became an NBA All-Star Game head coach in 2023, then won the NBA title in 2024 and got the Coach of the Year award in 2026. Outside of basketball, the 6-foot-2 former point guard also finds time to train various martial arts. Interestingly enough, the 38-year-old likened his recent Brazilian jiu-jitsu (BJJ) blue belt promotion to his biggest career achievement in basketball. “I don’t apply the grappling as much (in coaching) as I apply the mindset, and exposing myself to myself. It’s funny, we were fortunate enough to win (an NBA title) in 2024. I had the same feeling the day I got promoted to my blue belt as I did when I won the championship,” Mazzulla said in an interview with Daniel Cormier. “Oh c’mon!” the former UFC champion responded with a chuckle. The first step after white belt seemed trivial compared to an NBA world championship, after all. But Mazzulla, who was once described by NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown as “a psycho in a good way,” continued to explain why he was dead serious about his statement. “It was a feeling of like, what the f— am I going to do now? Now I got to figure out how to do this again,” Mazzulla explained. “There’s such a small space between genius and insanity, there’s such a small space between champion and ultimate failure… I’ll never forget the day I actually got promoted.” After getting badly worked in a training session, Mazzulla described a common feeling people get while progressing through the ranks in jiu-jitsu. “I’m getting the s— kicked out of me… I’m like ‘well, today is not the day. I’m not going to get it.’ (but) I get it,” Mazzulla said about receiving his blue belt. “Then I look around the gym. Now I’m stuck in this space of like I could lose at any time to a white belt, and I’m so far away from the best blue belt. “That day that I got (my blue belt), I wasn’t happy,” the NBA coach said. “I was more like ‘now I got to figure out how to do this.’ Fear came, anxiety came, paranoia came. Like now I’m not good enough anymore. Literally it was just one change and it changed everything. “I feel like that’s where I am as a coach. I have a taste of what it’s like (to be a champion), but now I’ve lost and I could go back to this… the (opposite) side of greatness,” he explained. “So I use that same perspective to push myself to hopefully take that into the team.” Mazzulla also reportedly tries to train around his busy NBA travel schedule, finding a gym on the road to train in the morning, before having a game in the evening. Apart from grappling, Mazzulla was also recently seen working on his striking recently at the famed Xtreme Couture gym. stories.title: Bucks adjust home opener to avoid World Series time conflict
stories.summary: The Bucks are going to have an afternoon tipoff for their Oct. 23 home opener with the Bulls to avoid a direct conflict with Game 1 of the World Series.
stories.detailText: MILWAUKEE -- The Milwaukee Bucks are going to have an afternoon tipoff for their Oct. 23 home opener with the Chicago Bulls to avoid a direct conflict with Game 1 of the World Series, which is taking place in Milwaukee that evening. The Bucks announced Friday that their home opener would take place at 3 p.m. CT rather than 7 p.m. Bucks officials said they worked with the NBA office to make the schedule change possible. The Milwaukee Brewers will host the Cleveland Guardians or Tampa Bay Rays in Game 1 of the World Series that night. The Brewers clinched their first World Series berth since 1982 on Thursday. "The Brewers' return to the World Series for the first time in 44 years is a special moment for Milwaukee and sports fans across Wisconsin," the Bucks said in a statement. "Congratulations to the Brewers and the entire organization on this tremendous achievement, and we'll be cheering them on as they begin their World Series run. The Bucks are proud to move our home opener to 3 p.m. in recognition of this historic occasion and thank the NBA for making this schedule change possible." The Bucks are opening their season Wednesday at Washington . The Bucks also have another potential World Series scheduling issue. They're scheduled to host the Cleveland Cavaliers the night of Oct. 31, which is when Game 7 would take place in Milwaukee if the World Series goes the distance.

Saint Thomas and Duke Miles were both waived, with Cris Carroll and Taye Fields then signed to similar Exhibit 10 contracts. The Sixers have signed Cris Carroll and Taye Fields to Exhibit-10 contracts, a team source told ESPN. Saint Thomas and Duke Miles were waived earlier today in a corresponding move. Carroll, a 6-6 forward, averaged 17.4 points on 39.6% from 3 last season for Youngstown State. — Dave McMenamin (@mcten) October 16, 2026 Thomas appeared in all three preseason games for the Sixers, with Miles taking the floor twice. Taye Fields is a 6-foot-4 guard out of North Alabama who spent last season with the Hefte Helfen Bulls in Austria’s Basketball Superliga. He participated in NBA Summer League with the Sixers a few months ago, averaging 2.0 points and 3.8 rebounds in 14.7 minutes across the five games. Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge. For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility. The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20. No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr. 's contract. "I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that." The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason. Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant Portland Trail Blazers ' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday. "Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. "I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent." Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant. Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton" Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season. "He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. "Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks." Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season. Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey . "It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there." Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season. "I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said. Harper addresses role for coming season After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season. "Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in." First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team: "Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language." LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win. "Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything" Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings. "I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors." Haliburton: I am 100% healthy Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season. "I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year." Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team. In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors. Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room. "We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room." "I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control." And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done." Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday. Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft. Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said. The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer. By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million. For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer. Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski . James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. "[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump." Grizzlies waive Russell The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.summary: The Lakers may be in the market for another backup center
stories.detailText: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 05: Jericho Sims #00 of the Milwaukee Bucks looks on against the Minnesota Timberwolves during the preseason NBA game at Fiserv Forum on October 05, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images As it currently stands, the Los Angeles Lakers’ center room features Walker Kessler, Kevon Looney and Sandro Mamukelashvili . Kessler, of course, is a locked-in starter while Looney and Mamukelashvili will split time as the reserves depending on matchups and game flow, given Mamukelashvili is a small-ball 5 and Looney is the traditional option. But according to Jake Fischer , it doesn’t sound like the Lakers are content to enter the season with just those three as their big man rotation. Fischer reports they’ve been linked to a bouncy Eastern Conference center in an aim to also trim down the roster. “The Lakers, meanwhile, have been engaged in trade talks to try to get their roster down from 16 to 15 standard contracts and perhaps even acquire some additional frontcourt help in the process,” Fischer wrote. “League sources say that the Lakers and Bucks have held exploratory trade discussions on a framework that would ship former first-round selection Dalton Knecht to Milwaukee (along with second-round draft capital) in exchange for big man Jericho Sims,” Fischer continued. “Yet it must be said that I’ve also heard some pessimism from sources briefed on those talks that such a trade will actually go through.” Now entering year six, Sims has spent time with both the New York Knicks and Milwaukee Bucks but hardly entrenched himself as a rotation player at either spot. He did, however, appear in a career-high 67 games last season en route to a career-high 1,318 minutes. He’s a sprightly, athletic, undersized center whose offensive arsenal is very limited beyond dunks and plagued by turnovers (career 24.1% turnover rate). It should not be undersold how dominant of a dunker he is, though. According to Basketball Reference, nearly 60% of all his made field goals (59.5%) have been dunks; he’s totaled 250 of them across five seasons, averaging just under one per game and one every 15.6 minutes. Furthermore, 82.1% of his career shots have come between 0-3 feet and he’s converted 80.3% of them. Alongside Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves, his above-the-rim play-finishing could have value in a small role, and he’s a pretty lively mover whose defensive imprint is often undone by poor positioning and underwhelming size at 6 feet 10 inches. Acquiring Sims wouldn’t likely be much of a needle-mover for Los Angeles. But it would diversify the center room a bit, bring in an efficient play-finisher who helps generate a good deal of offensive rebounds and offer Sims the most favorable offensive environment of his career. That could help on the margins. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.detailText: The Detroit Pistons are headed in the right direction as the preseason concludes. Jalen Duren saw preseason minutes, and man, did the Minnesota Timberwolves feel his presence. He ragdolled whoever, whenever. The Toronto Raptors function much differently than the newly formed run-and-gun Wolves, but we will see if Detroit gets the full version of Toronto tonight. After a 122-120 loss to the New York Knicks last night, how many starters play is in question for the Raptors. This is their last preseason game too, so maybe we get a mucked up first half with two of the projected stingiest defenses. GAME VITALS Where: Little Caesars Arena, Detroit, MI When: 7:00 PM EST Watch: TV20 Detroit/DAZN-DET Odds: Pistons (-9.5) That’s how you respond to noise, JD. Whether the sound alarms were self-inflicted or not is irrelevant now. You’ll win over skeptics with performances like that, while carrying it over to the playoffs. But we’re taking it game by game. He treated the Timberwolves like he was a D1 player returning to their high school, scrimmaging against the JV kids. From the opening tip, it was curtains. Slick right-to-left push dribbles, aggressive up-at-the-level defense, and a “what a future Detroit has” lob to Ausar in transition. Those first few minutes got you out of your seat. The lob to Ausar was an exclamation point because it showed what this team can be. This Pistons build goes as far as those two go. Cade is going to be an MVP candidate (and winner) for a long time. An aggressive, better-defending Duren and all-around threat Ausar will take this team to another level. The more Ausar can initiate the offense while being a threat defenses respect, the more freed up Cade will be. You love to see that instinctive behind-the-back dribble leading to a Duncan Robinson trey ball. That’s who Ausar can be! While the Raptors are still filling out their roster, we may see more reserves fighting for a spot tonight. On the key player front, their Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes, and Collin Murray-Boyles lineups will not be pleasant for anyone. That’s a hellacious defensive nucleus. Hopefully Isaiah Joe can get some string music going tonight if the Pistons reserves play extended minutes. I won’t overreact to his preseason slump because historically he’s a can’t-leave guy. He’ll snap out of it, and teams will forever treat him like the career 40 percent range shooter he his. His two-point scoring is intriguing because he might be the guy taking grenade shots in certain lineups. We’re going to see how much wiggle he has with an expanded role quickly. Ron Holland, Kevin Huerter, Paul Reed, Daniss Jenkins, Javonte Green, and Ebuka Okorie need to be plus-contributors for Detroit to go further than last year. We’re monitoring Holland’s offensive growth and Huerter’s shooting. Both have clear pathways to scale up there. Should we expect Okorie to get unlimited run on a team contending for a Larry O? No, but his microwaveness could swing games in certain spots. Detroit’s identity is still intact. They’re physical across the board and can now run more offensively slanted lineups. With J.B. Bickerstaff’s defensive principles, it’s hard to imagine any Detroit lineup trotting out a *bad* defense. They have some pieces to play with and can sacrifice some D for more offensive juice. Those things will be ironed out as the season progresses, but for now, we get through the preseason finale and get ready for the real thing. stories.detailText: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 15: Jalen Brunson #11 of the New York Knicks drives against Immanuel Quickley #5 of the Toronto Raptors during the fourth quarter of a preseason game at Madison Square Garden on October 15, 2026 in New York City. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Toronto Raptors fell to the New York Knicks 120-122 at Madison Square Garden. Despite coming off a 50-point victory against the Knicks on Tuesday, the Raptors couldn’t produce a similar performance. The Knicks fielded a significantly stronger lineup tonight, which featured their usual starting five, except for guard Josh Hart, who did not suit up due to injury. The Raptors would do the same, starting the same five from the last game. Raptors forward Scottie Barnes would get things started, scoring nine out of the 12 baskets and going 4/4 from the field. Both teams continued to trade baskets as the quarter progressed. The Knicks were finding a lot of success with their ball movement, whereas the Raptors ‘ three-point shooting was difficult to slow down. The Knicks would carry a three-point lead into the break. The second quarter showed the Knicks bench carrying the load as they jumped out to a quick eight-point lead. The Raptors eventually found their footing and would battle back. Barnes remained the focal point for the Raptors as he would continue to play well. He finished the half with 15 points, two rebounds, and three assists, while being 6/10 from the field and 3/3 on three-pointers. For the Knicks, centre Karl-Anthony Towns was giving the Raptors all sorts of trouble with his scoring ability in the paint and his flashy passes, contributing to the 63-58 halftime lead. Coming out of half, it was a committee of Raptors, including forward Kawhi Leonard and former Knicks duo RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley, who would contribute to an eight-point lead. The Raptors had more success on offence when Quickley, Barrett, Leonard, Barnes, and centre Collin Murray-Boyles were the five on the floor, something to keep an eye on when the regular season starts. The quarter would resume with both teams trading baskets, though Toronto looked to be the stronger team. This would be the case until New York exploded for a nine point unanswered run late in the frame to take the 87-79 lead into the final quarter of play. The final quarter of play started with both teams still having their strongest lineup out there. Barnes and Barrett would continue to add to their strong outings, though it seemed that everything the Raptors did well, the Knicks would do even better. Both teams would opt to put in bench players late in the game to give them valuable minutes. This would prove worthy to the Raptors, as guard Malachi Smith would hit two crucial three-pointers and a three point play from second-round pick Jaden Bradley would cut the Knicks lead to two. A crucial backcourt violation error for New York would give the Raptors a great opportunity to win the game, though some inspiring Knicks defending would shut the door as time out run out. An unfortunate result for the Raptors tonight as they played well for the majority of the game. They struggled heavily with on-court communication. Barnes (23 points, three rebounds, four assists and four blocks) and Barrett (21 points, eight rebounds, four assists) were the Raptors standouts and the younger guys in the squad showed reliability, resulting in some positive takeaways from tonight’s match. The Raptors will have one more preseason game to fix their mistakes as they take on the Detroit Pistons on Friday. Tip-off is set for 7 pm.

The Knicks wrapped up the preseason with their most solid performance, defeated the Raps in New York, and will next see the banner(s) rise to the rafters of MSG. Here’s the latest from everybody and their mothers. Mike Brown was asked about Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond and didn't know KAT was one assist shy of a triple-double 😂 "He was waving me off, KAT is such a nice guy, I was gonna wave back" pic.twitter.com/elHMtbCFYp — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 16, 2026 Mike Brown On the Knicks’ progress over the past year heading into their title defense: “I’m going to keep it real that there’s something in front of us. I’m not a fan of having an elephant in the room. I’ll address it: It’s about the process. It’s not about the end result. We can’t think about the end result right now. We have a ways to go. This is a new season, new team and we’re gonna have challenges in front of us. “It’s like climbing a mountain. Sometimes you go a 100 yards, but you might get knocked back five yards. Hopefully, it’s not 50 yards, but you might get back five or 10 yards, and you regroup as a team, and you figure out how to keep going forward the right way. “But making sure we embrace the process without slippage in that is going to be huge. And if I see us slipping up, it’s my job to let us know as a team that we’re off track. We need to get back on hopefully sooner than later.” On why Jalen Brunson is the NBA’s best leader, as voted by GMs: “He studies the game, and that helps a lot because you can always grow in any field you do. But he walks the talk. He works extremely hard, and he strives for perfection from himself. And when you do that, your peers see you do that, and you’re looked upon as the best player on the team, and it gives you credibility to tell somebody else when they’re not given their all or when they need to do this a little bit better or that a little bit better.” On Brunson’s toughness and willingness to hold teammates accountable: “He’s not afraid because, as a leader, sometimes you can be on an island because you have to always be conscious of ‘I got to do more, I got to do more’ in terms of work harder, focus, everybody’s going to make mistakes, but those little things. And so when you tell your teammates, they can get pissed at you, or they can be like, ‘hey, screw him because who is he to tell me what to do?’ And so you have to have some thick skin because it’s not going to always be you telling somebody to do something, then they embrace it. And I think Jalen has that thick skin and a toughness about him to be in a seat like this.” On Brunson potentially becoming an NBA head coach after his playing career: “I think Jalen has that thick skin and toughness about him to be in a seat like this. You won’t need to, though. My view? If you don’t want to… It’s up to you, Jalen.” On what he expects from the Knicks’ final roster spot: “If one of those guys makes our team, at least right now, they may not even play seven minutes — you know, seven straight minutes. And then at the end of the day, we just have to make a decision.” On the mentality required from the Knicks’ third-string center: “We just hope that there’s a passion and an energy and a focus coming from that spot because, I’m sure at times that person will start, at times they may be the first backup and at times they may be second backup. So as the minutes are fluctuating, you’re going to have to generate some internal energy at times, to go play in a low-minute game. “Sometimes he’ll maybe not play one or two, maybe three games in a row. You look for that, and then you know, you just look for somebody that’s going to play hard at the end of the day – try to do the things that you’re asking on both sides of the floor. And bring a little something different than what the two guys in front of you bring.” On Bruce Brown’s experience, toughness and versatility: “Bruce has been through a lot with a lot of different teams at a pretty high level. His toughness, his experience, his feel, all those things — he’s a winner. It seems like every place he’s gone, he’s won, but all those things can add a lot to the program, and then he’s versatile both ends of the floor. He could play a few different positions offensively; he can guard a few different positions defensively. So a guy like that, especially a veteran winner, can be helpful to any team.” On James Wiseman’s potential and development: “He’s young, he’s talented, you know, he’s raw, still. I think he’s still trying to establish a foothold in this league. But with the God-given attributes he has, in terms of athleticism and length and quickness, [they] can bode well for him on both ends of the floor. And at 25 years old, he hasn’t even reached his prime, especially knowing he hadn’t played a ton of basketball; having a vertical threat at the rim will help [the Knicks], or could help everybody else play the game a little bit easier, whether it’s driving the basketball or playing pick and roll.” Bill Pidto: "Banner's going up Tuesday night…What's it gonna be like here?" Jalen Brunson: (Looks up) pic.twitter.com/6BGxtrD5Sf — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) October 16, 2026 Jalen Brunson On his recovery from wrist surgery: “I had nine different casts. I was able to take it off if I ran or worked out with it. So I had one for workouts, one for showering and obviously one for everyday use.” On maintaining the Knicks’ championship-winning approach entering a new season: “I think what’s most important is that last year we took everything one day at a time. We were talking about — obviously, the topic was getting back to the conference finals and trying to advance. And I think for us now, the way we approached it last year was to take it one day at a time, every single day. So not talking about certain things. “Obviously, we know what it takes, but just going into this with the same mindset for this journey. Even though it’s a new journey, it’s a different journey; the approach has to be the same, if not better. “The first couple of weeks of the season is going to show us who we are and where we are. No matter what we’re doing, whether we’re playing great, playing bad, how are you going to be able to learn? And so, I mean, we’ll find a way. We’ll hold each other accountable, just like we did last year, and then we’ll be better.” On the Knicks’ preseason progress and preparing to defend their championship: “Each game got better and better. Just happy to be back. I feel like it’s a learning experience for us. We have to turn the page on last year and figure out how to get better every single day. It’s gonna be a different journey for us. Our mindset has to be different, and we’ll be ready to go.” Karl-Anthony Towns laughed when asked if he wanted to stay in tonight's game to try for a triple-double "I will not use my quote again" pic.twitter.com/wz1v9k3EVY — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 16, 2026 Karl-Anthony Towns On the Knicks’ preseason finale and preparing for opening night: “I thought today was a good dress rehearsal. It was cool, it was very nice to get back out there and get back into our flow and be really good. Obviously we have a lot of things to work on. But it was a good way to end the preseason.” On how he feels physically and his rhythm entering the regular season: “Yeah, I feel good. I feel really, really good.” On who’s the biggest complainer to referees among Knicks: “Josh Hart. Why’d y’all laugh? Did y’all agree with that or something? Everyone behind the camera, I just want y’all to know: y’all just clowned Josh Hart. That’s crazy for y’all to say — in New York, too.” On choosing between winning another NBA championship and a World Series: “Win a World Series, for sure. I already won an NBA championship.” On his pregame routine: “Before the game starts, I always give everyone at the table, including the fans behind, a chance to really get into the game. Just giving everybody a fist bump down the line of the table, and then go on the court.” On his favorite all-time big man: “I think Hakeem. I feel like, in a way, he kind of is mythical, like Wilt Chamberlain… but I’ve been able to talk and meet Hakeem, and he’s an amazing, amazing human.” On @Honda SportsNite, @IanBegley joins @emacSNY to discuss his prediction for the final Knicks roster spots, what stood out in the preseason, what to look for as the Knicks start the season, and the anticipation for raising a banner at Madison Square Garden pic.twitter.com/h7H0HUzPmD — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 16, 2026 Ian Begley On the Knicks’ roster decisions involving Bruce Brown, James Wiseman, Pacome Dadiet and Tyler Kolek: “Brown and James Wiseman have made it through preseason cuts. The Knicks clearly like both players. But New York only has room under the second apron in team salary to keep one player. In order to keep both Brown and Wiseman, the Knicks would need to trade a player on a standard contract without taking back salary. “My read heading into the weekend: Wiseman is a lock to make the roster. There is strong support to add Brown as well. The Knicks would need to make a trade by Monday afternoon if they want to keep Brown. I think they will explore all avenues to make that happen. “It’s logical to assume that the Knicks will move third-year wing Pacome Dadiet. stories.title: Sixers ready to continue building chemistry in final preseason game vs. Celtics
stories.summary: With the starting five set to back in action together, there’s plenty to focus on in the Sixers’ final preseason game against the Celtics.
stories.detailText: BROOKLYN, NY - OCTOBER 8: Tyrese Maxey #0 and LeBron James #23 of the Philadelphia 76ers talk during the game against the Brooklyn Nets on October 8, 2026 at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Sixers may have been beaten 144-106 on Saturday against the Celtics, but there were still the kinds of positives you want to see from Philly’s young guys as most of the starting five sat out. As their preseason finale approaches on Friday evening with a rematch against the Celtics, we’ll see if they can end things on a high note as their new stars are set to make another appearance. While we don’t know exactly how much we can expect to see the Sixers’ starting five on Friday, we should be getting a look at the new group at least until the early second half, according to Nick Nurse when he gave an update after Thursday’s practice. Nick Nurse on his plans RE: starters for the final preseason game: "The plan is we would like to get the majority of them into the second half…Then it's probably fairly short after that." pic.twitter.com/BoNmhIXNDn — Derek Bodner (@DerekBodnerNBA) October 15, 2026 Nurse originally mentioned wanting to get the starting group to play a couple of games in the preseason, so it makes sense for LeBron James, Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown to return and get a final tuneup before the regular season begins. Even in a preseason setting with lower minutes, it’ll be interesting to see how fluid their cutting and passing looks, how they continue pushing in transition, how others move off the ball while LeBron initiates, and generally how their initial chemistry looks as this group gets started together. In their brief half together against the Nets, the starters’ offense looked electric with so much firepower and range of styles to attack. Will we see more of the same against the Celtics? The Sixers' new Big 5 — LeBron, Embiid, Brown, Maxey and Edgecombe — played (preseason) together for the first time tonight. Here's a glimpse into the pace they played with, the offensive progression, off-ball movements and more in a highlight reel of the 5 together ⬇️🔥 pic.twitter.com/LYdWew3UNH — Erin Grugan (@eringrugan) October 9, 2026 Pure talent alone may carry the offense as the team starts to gel, although the defense may understandably take more time as schemes and communication are polished. That could lead to another strong showing from Jayson Tatum on Friday, after he calmly dropped 23 points on Saturday, with Payton Pritchard leading the team with 25 points and doing most of his damage from range with five made triples. Apart from seeing the starting group, there’s VJ Edgecombe to focus on who stood out yet again in the Sixers’ last game. He scored a team-high 19 points on 6-of-11 shooting with a pair of threes, plus three rebounds, four assists and four steals. Energetic, impactful and disruptive as always, Edgecombe played exactly how the team would hope. Jabari Walker continued his strong preseason on Saturday, too. He added 14 points on 6-of-11 shooting with six rebounds and a pair of assists. Walker stepping up comes at a good time as well, what with Ariel Hukporti’s injury shortening the Sixers’ center rotation. As Nurse inevitably experiments with different looks and mixes in more smaller lineups, especially when Embiid misses time, Walker is starting to make his case to be in the mix for more minutes. We have to keep a close eye on Labaron Philon as well. On Saturday against Boston, he flashed his silky jumper both off the catch and when creating off the bounce, tallied seven assists to only two turnovers with crisp passing, and finished with 14 points (albeit on modest 5-of-13 shooting) and a 4-of-8 mark from three. Even with how stacked their starting lineup is and how they can stagger stars, the Sixers need spark-plug ball-handling, shooting and playmaking off their bench. Philon has such clear upside to be a factor there. Basically, from the starting five chemistry to young guys like Philon, there’s plenty to monitor in the Sixers’ preseason finale. Whatever happens with Friday’s result, though, the main thing that matters is we’re only four days away from the start of real Sixers basketball. On Oct. 20, when they open the regular season against the Knicks, we’ll get our first look at LeBron and Co. playing real NBA action. It’s going to be quite the season.
