stories.title: What Brandin Podziemski learned from studying Jalen Brunson this offseason
stories.summary: After signing a five-year contract extension, Brandin Podziemski looks to add to his offensive game by analyzing the 2025-26 Finals MVP.
stories.detailText: What Brandin Podziemski learned from studying Jalen Brunson this offseason originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area After a career-best scoring season, Warriors guard Brandin Podziemski was busy learning from NBA champion Jalen Brunson’s film during the offseason. Talking with NBC Sports Bay Area’s Bonta Hill and Dalton Johnson on “Dubs Talk,” Podziemski highlighted how he and trainer Dustin Van Lieu were focused on Brunson’s game and style of play. “I know offseason this year was big on Jalen Brunson,” Podziemski said. “Being able to see him play a variety against defenses of different sorts, whether it was the (San Antonio) Spurs or the (Philadelphia) 76ers or whomever you want to call it, just seeing him having to manipulate different coverages and being successful and winning a championship. I think we took a lot from him this off-season and implemented it.” Podziemski and Brunson are both stockier left-handed guards, and Podziemski said he specifically studied Brunson’s ability to handle the Spurs’ “full-court” defense during the NBA Finals that the New York Knicks won 4-1. “We looked at a lot of concepts like that, how (Brunson) does that and keeps and creates the advantage,” Podziemski said. “That’s probably the biggest thing we’ve looked at besides obviously the footwork.” While Podziemski remains a polarizing figure among Warriors fans, his contract and underlying metrics reflect a productive player who has his organization’s trust. Coach Steve Kerr called him a “big part” of the Warriors’ future, exemplified by the five-year, $110 million extension Podziemski signed on Oct. 10. Podziemski played all 82 games in the 2025-26 season, averaging a career-high 13.8 points to go along with 5.1 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game. He also ranked fourth in the NBA with 0.28 charges drawn per game. More importantly, his presence on the floor next to Curry and Butler appears to be positive. Warriors lineups with Curry and Podziemski posted a net rating of +5.7, while Podziemski- and Butler-led lineups were +10.5. Podziemski likely will have to reprise his larger scoring role with Butler only slated to return around the All-Star break and center Kristaps Porziņģis out indefinitely with an unspecified health issue. stories.title: Doc Rivers believes this Paul George trait could be contagious for Celtics
stories.summary: Rivers, who coached George with the Clippers, explains how the veteran forward will help Boston.
stories.detailText: Doc Rivers believes this Paul George trait could be contagious for Celtics originally appeared on NBC Sports Boston Former Boston Celtics head coach Doc Rivers had the same shocked reaction to the Jaylen Brown trade that most fans did — but he also believes the additions of Paul George, Mitchell Robinson, and Mike Conley Jr. can help the Celtics remain competitive in a beefed-up Eastern Conference. “I think everything [the Celtics] do is intentional. I really do,” said Rivers, who will serve as analyst this season for the NBA on NBC . “When the trade went down, I was like, ‘Whoa, this is an interesting trade,’ especially to the partner that they chose. I was like, ‘I’m glad Tommy Heinsohn is not around right now,’ doing anything with Philly, you know? “But, at the end of the day, when you take a step back from the shock, and you look at their team, it fits. I think their team is gonna be really good.” How important is fit in the NBA? “As a coach, I never worried about it, the fit thing. I was like, ‘I’m gonna make it fit, you know? I’m not giving up on talent,’” said Rivers. “But there’s so much more now with the NBA and the contracts. Like, when you’re taking up 70 percent of your [salary cap with two players] — it just doesn’t work in the NBA anymore. And so every team is scrambling, as you can see. And, to me, what [the Celtics’ front office has] done is they went for that fit and the financial construction. So I think what they did was pretty smart overall.” Here are more takeaways from Rivers on the 2026-27 Celtics (you can hear the full interview on the latest Celtics Talk podcast , which also features play-by-play legend Mike Tirico): PG’s overlooked value: Defense that changes everyone around him Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images Paul George’s defensive impact should be huge for the Celtics. Rivers coached Paul George during their time with the Los Angeles Clippers and thinks there’s one primary way that George can still impact winning at an advanced age in Boston. “The thing I think you’re gonna be surprised with is his defense,” said Rivers. George has since piled up a team-high 7 steals in 49 minutes of preseason action, routinely sparking fast break opportunities after turning over opponents. “On ball, [Clippers teammate] Kawhi [Leonard] was better, but I remember [Clippers current head coach and former Rivers assistant] Ty Lue and I talking one night and I was like, ‘You know, Paul’s an elite defender, and I think he’s even better off the ball.’ What’s happening is elite off-the-ball defenders can be contagious.” George generated 2.7 steals and a staggering 6.5 deflections per 100 possessions last season with Philadelphia, ranking in the 97th percentile at his position for both marks. George has ranked in the 89th percentile or better in steal rate for his position in each of the past five seasons. On the offensive end, Rivers believes George can be maximized as a catch-and-shoot option. “He’s a great shooter. And where Jaylen did a lot off the dribble, I think Paul George they use far more as a catch-and-shoot guy. I think he’s elite at that,” said Rivers. “He can take you off the dribble, too. I didn’t use him as that much, when I was with the Clippers, because I wanted him to be catch and shoot. I think he’ll be more back to that catch and shoot stuff.” George shot 41.6 percent on 4.5 catch-and-shoot 3-pointers per game last season with Philadelphia (compared to 34.1 percent on 2.2 pull-up 3s per game). The shot defied him a bit in his preseason appearances, but it’s clear the attention that players like Jayson Tatum and Payton Pritchard can attract on drives will lead to many open catch-and-shoot looks for George. The D-White bounce back Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Can Derrick White improve his 3-point shooting this season? Rivers admitted there’s a bunch of potential X-factors for the Celtics this season, but the primary one is Derrick White finding his shot again. “I think Paul George’s health, I think Mitchell Robinson’s ability to rebound is still underestimated — and I think Derrick White returning back to Derrick White,” Rivers said when asked about X-factors. “[White] didn’t have his typical playoff run, he struggled with his shot. That’s a fluke. So I think Derrick White being back to Derrick White is huge.” Why is Rivers bullish on White finding his stroke again after the shooting woes of a year ago? ‘It’s the NBA, man. Like you get to missing shots and the NBA doesn’t stop and wait for you to get your mind right, you know?” said Rivers. “It just keeps going and there’s times you get left behind, mentally, and I thought that it was as simple as that.” More Doc thoughts –Doc loves Joe Mazzulla and his coaching style: “He’s one of my favorites. I mean, he really is, and not because he’s a Celtic. I just love him. I love him because he is who he is and I love coaches like that. You’re not going to talk him out of it. And that makes him a really good, consistent coach.” –East is wide open — but also incredibly daunting: ” I think the East is wide open. And unfortunately, it’s wide open meaning there’s five teams that I can rattle off that could win the East. In two years, it went from the worst conference to the best conference. And so I think that’s the tough part. I don’t think any team will win as much as they won last year. I also think there’s no tanking teams this year, so you can’t just count 15 wins, you know? So this is gonna be a hard NBA season for the East. View this post on Instagram –He’s got one bone to pick with Paul Pierce and Kevin Garnett: “You know what pisses me off? Paul and Kevin are golfing now. Like, what the heck? That would have been so much more fun … They ridiculed Ray and I for golfing, and now they love it, especially Paul. Paul plays every day.”

stories.summary: This is the last chance before the results count, so who will step up and lead the team tonight?
stories.detailText: DETROIT, MI - MARCH 31: Collin Murray-Boyles #12 and RJ Barrett #9 of the Toronto Raptors high five during the game against the Detroit Pistons on March 31, 2026 at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Chris Schwegler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Tonight the Raptors’ final preseason game tips off, this time against the Detroit Pistons. So far, Toronto has split the preseason with a 2-2 record. They started off-balance when they lost handily to the Heat, but followed it up with convincing wins over the Clippers and Knicks and a single-possession loss to the Knicks yesterday. The Pistons are 2-1 in the preseason. Detroit will have both a homecourt and rest advantage, having played their last contest on Wednesday. With this being the last preseason game though, it’s likely the benches will be cleared to cement final roster decisions for both teams before the official start to the season. Plus, both teams still have things they need to work on. One of the bigger themes of the preseason has been Toronto’s size and rebounding issues. In both losses they were beaten on the boards, and in both wins they controlled them. Not insignificant, especially given their lack of traditional depth at center. This could be a point of concern tonight as Detroit has size and rebounding power. Jalen Duren was 6th in the League last year in rebounds per game, supported by Cade Cunningham, John Collins, and Ausar Thompson who all averaged more than 5 rebounds per game as well. That, all before you even look at their bench or backups. To win the battle, we’ll probably see a lot of Collin Murray-Boyles tonight who has a great presence around the rim at both ends and seems to be able to read exactly where the ball is going. Scottie will have to step up too, especially when Poeltl is on the bench. Detroit has tooled their roster for size and space, with Duncan Robinson, Kevin Huerter, John Collins, and Isaiah Joe all strong shooters to complement and provide room to operate for Jalen Duren. Cade Cunningham has done a remarkable job distributing the ball and running their offence, always finding the open man and right play. He was second in the League last year on assists and hasn’t even hit his prime yet. Toronto’s defence has looked solid over the last couple of games, especially on the wings. This will be a great challenge for them, as plenty of teams around the League continue to develop similar offensive schemes. The Raptors’ offence has also been a lot more polished over the last few games, with Kawhi, RJ, and Scottie all taking turns leading the team in scoring. Quickley, CMB, Shead, Battle, Key, Burnett, and Walter have all managed double-digit performances. It would be a great way to start the season above .500 in the preseason. Where to Watch Tune in at 7pm ET on Sportsnet Probable Starters Toronto: Scottie Barnes, Jakob Poeltl, Immanuel Quickley, RJ Barrett, Kawhi Leonard Detroit: Duncan Robinson, John Collins, Jalen Duren, Cade Cunningham, Ausar Thompson Injury Status Toronto: Nate Bittle Detroit: None listed

teamStories.summary: With one preseason game left, here’s a look at the most encouraging and potentially worrying moments and performances.
teamStories.detailText: SALT LAKE CITY, UT - OCTOBER 12: Tarris Reed Jr. #10 of the San Antonio Spurs grabs the rebound during the game against the Utah Jazz during a 2026 NBA Preseason game on October 12, 2026 at Delta Center in Salt Lake City, Utah. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Melissa Majchrzak/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Who or what has impressed you the most during the Spurs’ preseason so far? Marilyn Dubinski: I was just hitting publish on an article about Tarris Reed’s impressive play when these questions came out, so I’ll change things up and go with Carter Bryant. He looks so much calmer and more comfortable, isn’t lost on defense, is contesting well without as much fouling, and while 6-12 from three while missing a game (as of Thursday) is not a huge sample size, his willingness to let it fly and lack of hesitation is a huge improvement over last season. Mark Barrington: I don’t know if you can learn much from preseason, especially since the Spurs haven’t let their starters play much, and they have looked pretty rusty for much of the time they’ve been on court. The biggest surprise for me has been Tarris Reed. I figured he’d be in the Spurs’ plans this season, but he’s making a case for being in the rotation on opening day. He’s the most NBA-ready rookie I’ve seen on the Spurs since … maybe Tim Duncan? There have been plenty of really good players that have started their careers in the Silver and Black uniform, but most of them weren’t quite fully developed when they arrived. I’m excluding Victor Wembanyama from this assessment, because his talent level defies analysis. Devon Birdsong: I won’t say that I’m surprised by how good Carter Bryant looks, after he held his own in the postseason as a rookie who had uneven regular season minutes, but he has looked every bit the 3-and-D forward of the future that the Spurs will need him to be. It’s easier to see with Harrison Barnes, but Tobias Harris is also into the back nine of his career, and age is, as always, undefeated. I loved seeing the Spurs inject youth into their big man rotation in the draft, but forward is such a critical position in this era of the NBA, and the Spurs proving they can still find contributors at that part of the draft (14th) and bolster the roster with young talent bodes well for a club with impending depth departures and cap gymnastics in their future. Jeje Gomez: The storyline I was the most excited to follow heading into preseason was the battle for minutes at the forward spots, and especially how Carter Bryant looked. So far, Bryant has impressed. There are no signs of a major leap that foreshadows stardom, but that wasn’t really what anyone was looking for. The main things he needed to show were the ability to play under control and to show not as much fear of shooting, and so far, he’s done well in both areas. Teams still leave him open often, but that’s just going to happen until he develops consistency as a marksman. I’m not sure if he’ll start the season getting major minutes, but he has looked like a genuine option. Have you seen anything so far that has you worried about the Spurs heading into the regular season? Dubinski: This is where you really can’t overreact to the preseason. It was easy to half-joke about the Spurs blowing yet another double-digit lead to open the preseason considering how the Finals went, but we’ll worry about that if it continues to be an issue in the regular season. I was also (jokingly) working to not let my Battered Aggie Syndrome from the way Texas A&M’s football season is going sneak over to the NBA side – from playoff team to this?! You better not do this to me too, Spurs! – but I know they’re just shaking off the rust, and they appeared to start finding their rhythm again by the home game against the Suns (albeit with none of Phoenix’s starters playing, but when talking about rhythm, opponent doesn’t matter). I trust they’ll be in form by the regular season opener. Barrington: I’m not worried! Yes, the level of play has been haphazard and inconsistent in preseason, which is basically meaningless. This team went to the Finals last year, and they might have a bit of a slow start to the regular season after a short off-season, but no team has ever won a championship before the All-Star Break*. [Except for the Knicks, who won the NBA Cup and then won the Larry O’Brien trophy, becoming the first team ever to win both in the same season.] This team is supremely talented, and Reed and Quaintance address the major weaknesses in the roster. Will this come together again in Mitch Johnson’s second full year as a head coach in the NBA? I think a lot of that depends on how well Billy Donovan can implement his system in his first year on the staff. I have a good feeling about that. Birdsong: I still have questions about that three-guard lineup (four, if you count Wemby) they’ve been trotting out, especially on the defensive end. Wemby’s going to be able to smother a lot, but teams with quality stretch bigs have figured out that they can scheme him to the perimeter. Now, that’s not a lot of teams, thankfully, but Spurs brass can’t just depend on Wemby to bail schemes out defensively. I need to see how that (and other) lineups/schemes fare in the regular season, but that’s about as nitty a pick as I can find for now. Preseason disclaimers aside, the team looks really locked in. We’ll know exactly how locked in (and schematically sound) they are soon enough. Gomez: Preseason can be a good gauge of how teams with a lot of roster turnover are gelling, but that’s not the Spurs, especially after Harris’ injury, so there’s not much to worry about. I’ll admit that since we know how they look when they are trying, I haven’t been watching the games as attentively as I do when they count, but I have noticed some up-and-down moments that are expected of a team that went so far in the playoffs and probably isn’t taking these games as seriously. The three-guard starting lineup is new, but it seems like it’s here to stay, so I’ll worry (or get excited) about it around 15 into the regular season, when we’ll have a better understanding of its strengths and weaknesses. Do you think preseason performances will change the projected rotation or result in a signing using the last roster spot? Dubinski: I don’t think there will be another signing right away considering they have to wait a bit to stay under the cap, but of all the players who weren’t rotation players last season, Reed is the one who will make Mitch Johnson have to start thinking. I don’t think he’ll be in the main rotation right away, but it should mean a shorter leash for Kornet, and Johnson shouldn’t hesitate to throw Reed out there against bigger centers that give Kornet trouble. Barrington: As I mentioned above, I believe that Tarris Reed has earned himself a spot in the regular rotation. Other than that, nobody has really distinguished themselves. I feel bad for David Jones-Garcia, who has played poorly in preseason. If he sticks as a two-way player, hopefully he can pick up his game during the season and earn more playing time. The Spurs aren’t going to fill that last spot with anyone on the preseason roster, but there’s always the chance that they’ll pick up a player that gets waived by another team. I feel like it’s most likely that they keep that spot open until the trading deadline so they can pick up a player for the playoff run if someone good becomes available. Birdsong: Maybe, but outside of Reed (who has all but locked down the role of 3rd big man), I don’t see much happening that isn’t due to injury. It’s a long season, so I fully expect there to be games where players like Reed and Bryant get a lot of run, but that extra slot feels like flexibility insurance. Whether for trade purposes or waiver pickups, who knows? I’m not sure it’ll matter much, because this team is so insanely deep that it would take a medieval plague for the Spurs to get desperate. *knocks on wood* Still, it’s fun to hypothesize. I choose to believe that they’ll hold it open in case Timmy decides to fundamentally flex on another generation, five minutes or so per game, just for fun. Gomez: I don’t see many changes to the rotation. I really doubt a couple of preseason performances would change the plan to go with the three-guard starting lineup; the battle at forward is intriguing, but no one has played so well as to separate themselves from the pack; Reed is a beast, but I doubt he’ll beat out Kornet for backup center, at least to start. The one spot in which I can see a change is with the third two-way spot. The Spurs have gotten a really good look at David Jones-Garcia, and if they feel like they need more depth at a different spot or someone intriguing is available, I could see a world in which they give someone else a shot. But even that would surprise me. San Antonio seems ready for the season.

stories.title: Eagles' Saquon Barkley ruled out; DeVonta Smith to return
stories.summary: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers with a hamstring injury, but it appears WR DeVonta Smith will return.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- Eagles running back Saquon Barkley has been ruled out for Sunday's home game against the Carolina Panthers with a hamstring injury, but it appears receiver DeVonta Smith will make his return to the lineup. Smith does not carry an injury designation after missing the previous two games with a hamstring injury. "I'm good," Smith said when asked about the injury after practice Friday, adding that whether he plays is "up to the doctors." With Barkley, Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby all ruled out, Dameon Pierce is in line to get the bulk of the carries out of the backfield. Barkley exited early in the first quarter of the Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and has been sidelined since. Shipley was placed on injured reserve Friday with a foot injury, joining Bigsby (abdomen). Tanner McKee , meanwhile, is slated to start in place of quarterback Jalen Hurts , who was ruled out Thursday due to a superficial blood clot in his calf. Edge rusher Jonathan Greenard said he plans to test his ankle pregame, as he did in London before being ruled out against the Jaguars , though he carries no designation. Fellow edge rushers Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and AJ Epenesa (back) and safety Michael Carter (abdomen) have been ruled out. Linemen Landon Dickerson and Drew Kendall are questionable with knee injuries.

stories.title: Packers' Josh Jacobs eligible to return next week amid probe
stories.summary: Packers RB Josh Jacobs will be removed from the commissioner exempt list Monday, the league announced, making him eligible to practice and play next week.
stories.detailText: GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Packers running back Josh Jacobs will be removed from the commissioner exempt list Monday, the league announced, making him eligible to practice and play next week. The league's investigation into Jacobs under the personal conduct policy remains ongoing, however, leaving open the possibility that he could still be suspended. When he comes off the list next week, Jacobs will have missed the first six games of the season, and those games would count toward any suspension. However, if Jacobs ends up getting suspended for more than six games, he would have to miss additional games to make up the difference. After playing the Cowboys this Sunday at Lambeau Field, the Packers will visit the Lions on Oct. 25. "Josh has dedicated the last several months to bettering himself, and he accepts responsibility for his actions," Jacobs' attorneys, Clarence F. Duchac III, David Z. Chesnoff and Richard A. Schonfeld, said in a statement. "He is excited to get back to work and on the field with his teammates. Josh is grateful for the support he is receiving from his teammates, coaches, the Packers organization, and the greatest fans in the world." Jacobs was placed on the commissioner exempt list Aug. 30 while the NFL continued to gather information about the May 23 incident with a woman at his home near Green Bay. Jacobs pleaded no contest Sept. 10 to charges of battery and criminal destruction of property. He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000 and agreed to a deferred judgment agreement on a charge of damage to property. The woman did not speak with the NFL upon request due to privacy concerns, one of her attorneys, Amir Tahmassebi, said. Jacobs, meanwhile, did speak to the league, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. Part of the reason the league has not closed its investigation is because it has not seen the surveillance video from Jacobs' home that was noted in the criminal report. The video showed the portion of the incident that occurred in Jacobs' garage but not from inside the house. On Sept. 24, Brown County (Wisconsin) Circuit Court judge Marc A. Hammer lifted a temporary seal of the records and turned the decision whether to release part or all of the records over to the Hobart/Lawrence (Wisconsin) police department. On Tuesday, the police department announced it would release some records but did not say whether the surveillance video was part of the documents it deemed available for public consumption. However, that release would be delayed pending appeals from the parties involved. On Wednesday, both Jacobs and the victim in the case filed suit to block the release of evidence and have it permanently sealed.

stories.title: Eagles poach QB from Cowboys amid Jalen Hurts blood clot uncertainty
stories.summary: With QB Jalen Hurts sidelined by a blood clot in his calf, the Philadelphia Eagles are signing an intriguing player from the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad.
stories.detailText: The Philadelphia Eagles plan to poach a quarterback from an NFC East rival in the wake of Jalen Hurts' unexpected injury . The Eagles are signing Joe Milton III off the practice squad of the Dallas Cowboys , according to multiple reports on Friday, Oct. 16. This was the start of Milton's second season with the Cowboys after being traded to Dallas by the New England Patriots in exchange for a fifth-round pick in April 2025 . NFL rules stipulate that a player signed off another team's practice squad must be placed on the 53-man roster. The Eagles are scheduled to host the Carolina Panthers in Week 6 action on Sunday. NFL WEEK 6: Game picks, odds and expert predictions for every matchup How Joe Milton fits with Eagles after Jalen Hurts injury The Eagles announced on Thursday that Hurts has a "superficial blood clot," that he is believed to have suffered during the team's Oct. 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams . He was cleared to play in Philadelphia's Oct. 11 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, England, before a follow-up ultrasound "revealed movement in the small blood clot." That led the Eagles to shut Hurts down for the immediate future. Before acquiring Milton, back-up Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton were the only other quarterbacks listed on the Philadelphia roster. McKee, 26, is slated to be the starter under center in Week 6 for the Eagles. He was the starting quarterback during the final game of the Eagles' regular season in each of the past two years and had a 1-1 record in those appearances. Payton was Philadelphia's fifth-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. If McGee were to falter and Hurts' absence forces an injured reserve stint, Milton could have an opportunity to start some games in Philadelphia. He's long been an intriguing developmental prospect because of his arm strength and could offer a downfield passing element to an offense that has struggled to generate explosive plays. Joe Milton stats Milton has never started an NFL game and has five career regular-season appearances over two seasons with the Patriots and Cowboys. Most of Milton's experience has come in the preseason, including several impressive moments in August with Dallas. Milton completed more than 67% of his passes over three 2026 exhibition games for 378 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. It included an eye-popping performance in his lone preseason start on Aug. 22 against the Arizona Cardinals in which he completed 9 of 13 passes for 179 yards and accounted for three touchdowns (two passing, one rushing). He won't be a long-term answer due to inconsistency and accuracy issues that have cropped up throughout his career. But Milton has shown enough promise to become a helpful stopgap until Hurts is back. It's a relatively low-risk move for the Eagles. stories.title: Decked-out, diehard Jaguars fans swarm London for pub takeover
stories.summary: Jaguars fans roll deep in the United Kingdom, and the fandom showed up big at London's briefly renamed ''Tealwood'' pub Thursday night.
stories.detailText: LONDON -- For three hours Thursday night, the Greenwood sports pub and kitchen on Victoria Street in Central London ceased to exist. In its place: Tealwood. An apt renaming, as Greenwood was hosting one of three pub takeover events sponsored by the Jacksonville Jaguars ' U.K. branch for Jaguars fans who live in the United Kingdom or made the trip to London for the team's annual home game at Wembley Stadium this Sunday. There will be another Friday night and Saturday afternoon, and there was one the previous Friday night in advance of the Jaguars' home game at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week, which they won 19-17 on Cam Little 's 57-yard field goal as time expired. Those events are part of the NFL franchise's movement to continue to build its international fanbase, a push that began back in 2013 when the team played the first of what is now 15 games in London. The Jaguars also have their own U.K. fan club (Union Jax), have been heavily involved in helping to build interest in flag football with clinics, have appearances with current and former players throughout the year, run a year-round junior cheerleading program and send hundreds of students annually to the London games as part of a Reward Rows program. "Even if you knew nothing about the NFL, you were like, 'Oh, but the Jags are our team,'" said Phoebe Schecter, a former Buffalo Bills coaching intern, one of the first members of the Great Britain national American football team and now an NFL analyst for Sky Sports. "And so I think there's always going to be that really great association. "The Jags really do have a presence [in the U.K.], and the fans are truly bought in, and you get superfans. I mean, something as silly as somebody's on social, it's like a Mr. and Mrs. Jaxson de Ville, but they're superfans here in the U.K. and they're bought into the costumes and this whole persona. It's who they are. And you see that in the States, and now that's kind of creeping in over here in a great way." Jamie Phillips and Francis Sweeney are two of those fans. Sweeney -- decked out in an oversized Jaguars hat, jersey and jacket and carrying a Jags-themed wrestling belt over his shoulder -- has attended the team's games in London for the past five years. He's not the only Jags fan in his family, though. "My wife doesn't like any sports, and she's obsessed with the Jaguars," he said. Phillips, who was at Thursday night's pub takeover, wore a Jaguars mascot fuzzy hat on the 59-degree day at the Jaguars' practice at The Grove resort, the team's headquarters since it arrived Oct. 9. He was the team's 2024 nominee for the NFL's International Fan of the Year and has been a Jaguars fan for 15 years. That began two years before the Jaguars started making annual trips overseas, but Phillips latched on to the franchise even though it had just three winning seasons since the 2000s began. "I want to take after the underdog as most Brits do," he said. "A bit of an obsession, really, is what it's become." Phillips and Sweeney were among the 200 fans who had tickets to attend Friday's practice. There were also dozens of students from multiple primary and secondary schools across the London area, all of whom participate in JagTag. That's the Jaguars U.K. -- an arm of the franchise based in the U.K. -- flag football program for people ages 8-18. As practice wound down, the students were getting ready to get onto the field, receive tips and run drills with the 16 members of the Jaguars' practice squad. The program involves 360 schools in six major cities and 12 towns around London. It began in 2016 with roughly 1,200 participants and in 2024 had reached 100,000, said Andy Scott, the U.K. grassroots manager of JagTag. "We started in about six schools in West London in Fulham because of our connection with [Jaguars] ownership," Scott said. "Obviously, our owner [Shad Khan] owns the Fulham Football Club, so we ran it out of the foundation to try and gain that footprint across there. So yeah, it was small steps to a big finish." Ben Conway and Joel Neumann also were at Friday's practice. The two run the social media account "Endzone Near You" on Instagram, TikTok and Facebook and produce daily NFL content. They're also huge Jaguars fans -- both were at the Jaguars' 19-17 victory over Philadelphia at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday, and they'll be at Sunday's game against the Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium. Their most notable post from the last game summarized the final 12 seconds: The reaction of Eagles fans around them after Jake Elliott's 48-yard field goal gave Philadelphia a 17-16 lead, followed by their reaction after Little's winning field goal as time expired. The final play of that game was among the season highlights playing on 17 television screens at Greenwood/Tealwood during Thursday night's pub takeover. The three-hour event included appearances by Jaguars cheerleaders and Jaxson de Ville. Schecter, along with former NFL cornerback and current Sky Sports NFL analyst Jason Bell and Jay Lawrence of Absolute Radio, a British national radio station, emceed the event. Fans in the two-story pub were decked out in assorted Jaguars gear, including the jerseys of cornerback Travis Hunter , quarterback Trevor Lawrence , tight end Brenton Strange and defensive end Josh Hines-Allen , as well as those of former players Fred Taylor and Keenan McCardell. The highlight of the night was a Jaguars trivia contest. Among the questions: What color jerseys did the Jaguars wear in their first appearance in London in 2013? Answer: Black. How many teams have the Jaguars played in London? Answer: 13 ( San Francisco , Dallas , Indianapolis , Baltimore , Houston , Denver , Atlanta , New England , the Los Angeles Rams , Miami and Chicago once, and Buffalo and Philadelphia twice). How long was the longest TD scored in international game history, and who scored it? Answer: Parker Washington on a 97-yard punt return. Schecter called the takeover, which has become a regular occurrence in London when the team is in town, a success. She hopes it will result in more people becoming Jaguars fans. "People want to be a part of something," she said. "They want to feel like they're part of a team. And I think the 'Duuuval' chant, the Jags, that's something that they feel like they can own."

stories.title: Bears' Caleb Williams questionable after 3 days of practice
stories.summary: The quarterback said there are several hurdles to clear before he would be able to face the Falcons on Sunday.
stories.detailText: LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Quarterback Caleb Williams was officially listed as questionable on the Chicago Bears ' final injury report ahead of their Week 6 game at the Atlanta Falcons ( Sunday, 1 p.m. ET, Fox ). Williams was a full participant during the Bears' Wednesday walk-through and practice sessions Thursday and Friday. The quarterback said he had to go through "a bunch of medical protocols" before being cleared by team trainers, which could happen before the team leaves for Atlanta. "I'm hopeful we'll have more clarity at the end of the day today," Bears coach Ben Johnson said Friday. "He looked good [Thursday] for one practice, but we've got to be able to stack a few back-to-back. He got some good work in on Wednesday, even though we walked through, he went through his own throwing session beforehand. Part of the plan, and he's on track right now." Williams missed three straight games while recovering from a hamstring injury sustained during the fourth quarter of a Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . On Thursday, he took issue with the reporting around his injury , for which he claimed that "nothing that has come out that has been right about what it is and what it has been." Johnson did not sense that his quarterback was frustrated with anything other than not being able to play. "I, honestly, I didn't feel any frustration from him," Johnson said. "He was in this little bit of a no-man's land, 'Hey, what do I what do with myself? I've never been in this situation. I've never been in the training room this much. I've never been second or third fiddle in the quarterback room ever in my life.' Just like, 'I just need a little guidance on how I can best help and serve.' "He's a captain, he wants to do that desperately. 'How can I help us win in this different setting?' I don't know that I felt frustration, other than an eagerness to get back out there and help the guys on the field." While Williams' status is questionable, the Bears will be without running back Kyle Monangai for a second straight game. Monangai did not practice this week while recovering from thumb and toe injuries, the latter of which he visited a specialist for last week. "It wasn't one of those things we felt like we needed to put him on IR for," Johnson said. "So, it's still week-to-week, and as far as I know he's trending in the right direction." Chicago will also be down three starters on defense, with defensive end Montez Sweat 's two-game suspension for violating the PED policy and injuries that are sidelining linebacker T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Dayo Odeyingbo (quad) in Week 6.

stories.title: Broncos' Jonathon Cooper off commissioner's exempt list, could return Week 7
stories.summary: Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper was removed from the commissioner's exempt list Friday, meaning he is available to play Week 7. Cooper, who was arrested twice in a seven-day span in June on domestic violence charges, has been on the list since Aug. 30.
stories.detailText: ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- NFL commissioner Roger Goodell removed Denver Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the league's exempt list Friday. Cooper, who was unable to practice or play in games while he was on the list, is now available to play the Broncos' Week 7 game against the Arizona Cardinals . Cooper, who was arrested twice in a seven-day span in June on domestic violence charges , has been on the exempt list since Aug. 30. Cooper was in Douglas County (Colo.) court last week for a motions hearing and now has a March 2-4 trial scheduled in his case, as well as a pre-trial hearing scheduled for Feb. 19 . In a statement Friday, the NFL said its review of Cooper's case "remains ongoing and is not affected by this change to Cooper's roster status.'' It means Cooper could still face league discipline at a later date under the NFL's personal conduct policy. The Broncos will get a one-week roster exemption for Cooper, who can now return to practice. He could then be added to the 53-man roster at any point over the next week and play Sunday against the Cardinals. He had been able to attend meetings and other team functions, including weight room and conditioning work, when he was on the exempt list. The exempt list is designed to remove a player from participation in games and practices while potential violations of the NFL's personal conduct policy are reviewed. Cooper has been paid while on the list. His time on the exempt list -- the first six weeks of the regular season -- could count toward any league-mandated suspension in the future. He would, however, if suspended, have to return the weekly game checks he has received because suspensions from the personal conduct policy are without pay. Cooper had practiced throughout training camp. Cooper faces a felony charge of second-degree assault by strangulation and three misdemeanors, including violating a protection order, after he was arrested June 4 and then again June 11 after incidents involving his girlfriend. The felony charge stemmed from the first arrest after the results of a forensic examination of Cooper's girlfriend by a nurse. The affidavit that was included in the police investigation into Cooper's first arrest included the report from the medical exam of Cooper's girlfriend. In it, a nurse wrote the woman experienced a physical injury from being choked that led to a "substantial risk of death" or substantial risk of injury, including the possibility of traumatic brain injury. Broncos coach Sean Payton has consistently deferred to the NFL's investigation and the legal process when he has discussed the team's approach with the sixth-year linebacker. Payton said the Broncos set guidelines for Cooper after the arrest and that has included therapy. Cooper was a seventh-round pick in the 2021 draft and has 31.5 sacks in 81 career games with the Broncos, including eight sacks last season. He has started every game in each of the past three seasons. The Broncos are 4-2 after Thursday night's win over the Seattle Seahawks .

stories.detailText: (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Green Bay Packers ruled out defensive lineman Jonathan Ford (calf), defensive lineman Javon Hargrave (Achilles), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle) and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) on Friday. None of these players will suit up against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, and the Packers will likely need to make roster moves to backfill for these injured players. Beyond the players ruled out, offensive lineman Aaron Banks (knee/toe), defensive lineman Anthony Campbell (ankle), cornerback Brandon Cisse (hip) and offensive lineman Jacob Monk (quadricep) are listed as questionable for Week 6. Receiver Savion Williams (ankle), whose IR practice window has opened up, is questionable, while defensive lineman Jordon Riley (Achilles), whose PUP practice window has opened up, is doubtful. With so many moving parts, let’s just lay out the Packers’ full roster (including players’ injury statuses) going into Sunday Night Football . Quarterback Jordan Love Tyrod Taylor Nothing is concerning here. Running Back MarShawn Lloyd Pierre Strong Jr. Kaleb Johnson Nothing is concerning here. Receiver Christian Watson Matthew Golden Skyy Moore (out) Bo Melton J. Michael Sturdivant The Packers almost always have five or more receivers on the 48-man game-day roster, so expect to see a move here with Moore already ruled out — be it the activation of Williams to the 53-man roster or a call-up for receiver Isaiah Neyor from the practice squad. It’s also possible that Green Bay places Moore on the injured reserve to free up a roster spot. Tight End Tucker Kraft Mark Redman Jonnu Smith Josh Whyle Nothing is concerning here. Offensive Line Jordan Morgan Laken Tomlinson Sean Rhyan Travis Glover Anthony Belton Aaron Banks (questionable) Kevin Zeitler Jager Burton Jacob Monk (questionable) Donovan Jennings Nothing is concerning here, considering the Packers will need to scratch three at the position anyway. Even if Banks and Monk can’t go, Green Bay will still need a healthy scratch at the position. Defensive Line Karl Brooks Devonte Wyatt Javon Hargrave (out) Chris McClellan Jonathan Ford (out) Anthony Campbell (questionable) This is red alert/it could cost the team the game levels of concern. The Packers need five interior defensive linemen to be able to keep guys fresh, but they only have three players on the 53-man roster who are absolutely 100 percent going to play on Sunday. Green Bay is going to need two of the following players to give them reps: Campbell (questionable), Riley (PUP, doubtful) and/or a practice squad player David Blay Jr. Edge Defender Lukas Van Ness Barryn Sorrell Brenton Cox Jr. Dani Dennis-Sutton Nothing is concerning here, unless the team gets the bright idea to move Lukas Van Ness to the interior defensive line to help their numbers issue there…which would leave the Packers with just three edge defenders for the entire game against Dallas. That’s one issue about moving LVN around. Off-Ball Linebacker Zaire Franklin Isaiah McDuffie Ty’Ron Hopper Nick Niemann Kristian Welch Nothing is concerning here. Cornerback Keisean Nixon Brandon Cisse (questionable) Carrington Valentine Benjamin St-Juste (out) Kamal Hadden The Packers probably want to keep five players at cornerback on the 48-man game-day roster this week, not because of defense but because Bo Melton is having to play more offense as Skyy Moore’s replacement, meaning a similar body type (likely a cornerback) will have to backfill for Melton on special teams. Thankfully, Keisean Nixon was cleared from his injury, but now Cisse could potentially miss action and St-Juste is guaranteed to miss action. At minimum, assume that rookie practice squad cornerback Domani Jackson gets activated for his first NFL game. Safety Xavier McKinney Evan Williams Javon Bullard Kitan Oladapo Specialists K Trey Smack P Daniel Whelan LS Matt Orzech — So what do the Packers need to add this weekend? One receiver IR: Savon Williams PS: Isaiah Neyor, Quincy Skinner Jr. and/or Coleman Owen One or two defensive linemen PUP: Jordon Riley PS: David Blay Jr. If the team can’t carry five defensive linemen without moving Lukas Van Ness over, look for practice squad edge rushers Nyjalik Kelly or Arron Mosby to potentially be called up. One or two cornerbacks PS: Domani Jackson and/or Elijah Culp Look for the team to make a decent number of moves on Saturday. Remember, Hargrave and Moore are IR candidates, the team already has an open roster spot on the 53 and the team has the option to use two practice squad elevations, too. There’s a bunch of different buttons they can press to get to a 48-man game-day roster. stories.title: Seahawks make unwanted NFL history in loss vs. Broncos
stories.summary: Seattle’s defense showed out but it was the offensive struggles that put Denver in the record books.
stories.detailText: While it was the defense that kept the Seattle Seahawks within striking distance right until the end in their devastating 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday night, it was ultimately Sam Darnold and the offense’s inability to string together scoring drives that helped their former AFC West rival make history. With just 168 yards of offense, the Broncos now hold the record for the lowest yardage total in an overtime win in NFL history, breaking a record that stood for 22 years. Or, put another way, the Seahawks hold the record for fewest yards allowed in an overtime loss in NFL history . They surpassed the 2004 Chicago Bears who defeated the Tennessee Titans 19-17 in Week 9 with 176 yards. The Broncos' 168 total yards of offense is the lowest yardage total in an overtime victory in NFL history pic.twitter.com/f14gCsv3Sh — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) October 16, 2026 It’s the second notable overtime win from a struggling offense this season, joining the Green Bay Packers Week 2 comeback win over the New York Jets, where they strung together just 199 total yards (5th lowest all time). Albeit, the game was played in rain and windy conditions, which likely contributed to the low scoring outcome. However, it wasn’t the weather that put Denver in a position to beat the defending Super Bowl champions, but rather a dominant performance from the defense, who racked up five sacks, two interceptions and two forced fumbles—one of which they recovered. Offensively, quarterback Bo Nix averaged an unfathomable 0.6 air yards per completion. Seattle struck first with a field goal at 8:29 in the opening frame, but after back-to-back second quarter touchdowns from running backs J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey put the Broncos up 14-3, their defense was able to hold it down. Wide receiver Rashid Shaheed fumbled on the ensuing drive, which resulted in a turnover and although Seattle’s defense forced a punt to give Darnold and company one more chance to put points up before halftime, nothing came of it. However, the Seahawks defense turned a corner in the second half. They forced punts on all Denver’s possessions but the offensive inconsistency continued, with a missed 47-yard field goal from kicker Jason Myers to open the third quarter followed by two consecutive punts. As a result, Nix and the Broncos remained in a position to control the clock and ultimately, they did. Even though they generated just two trips to the red zone all night, Sam Darnold’s costly interception in overtime set up Will Lutz’s game-winning field goal. The saying is defense wins championships and if last night was any indication, it sure does.

stories.title: Lions put OL Ben Bartch, WR Tom Kennedy, LB Devin White on injured reserve
stories.summary: The Lions took care of some roster business during their bye week.
stories.detailText: The Lions took care of some roster business during their bye week. They announced that they have placed offensive lineman Ben Bartch, wide receiver Tom Kennedy, and linebacker Devin White on the injured reserve list. All three players will have to miss at least four games before they'll have a chance to return. Bartch was inactive in Week 5 due to a foot injury and White broke his forearm in that game. Kennedy is expected to miss the rest of the season with an MCL injury that requires surgery. The Lions now have three open roster spots to fill. Safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays have designated for return from injured reserve, so they could take two of those slots.

stories.summary: Let’s take a look at the Panthers key roster moves and the injury report heading into this week’s matchup.
stories.detailText: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Keith Cooper Jr. #97 of the Miami Dolphins leaves the field after warmups against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Raiders defeated the Dolphins 27-13. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries Finally, some good news on the injury front! Through their 2-2 start this year the Panthers have distinguished themselves as the most injured team in the NFL and it’s impressive Carolina is playing .500 ball. Young stud wide receiver Jalen Coker is back after missing the Panthers last game. Running back Trevor Etienne has yet to make his 2026 debut and he is also listed as questionable after fully participating this week in practice. The biggest impact could be on the offensive line. Stalwart right tackle Taylor Moton has yet to play in 2026 due to blood clots and is listed as questionable after being a full participant in this week’s practices. Veteran guard Damien Lewis missed Carolina’s last game and is listed as questionable for Sunday but was a full participant in Friday’s practice. Also hoping to make his 2026 debut is veteran defensive tackle Tershawn Wharton who is now questionable with a neck injury. The Panthers bye last week gave other guys who have been dinged up to get some rest, including outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips and tight ends Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller. Right tackle Monroe Freeling is doubtful while running back AJ Dillon is out for Sunday. Transactions Signed DT Keith Cooper to the practice squad Cooper was a 2025 undrafted free agent who was signed by the Cleveland Browns and appeared in one game as a rookie with no stats. Earlier this year he joined the Miami Dolphins and has played in three games in 2026 with one tackle. Cooper played 29 defensive snaps and 16 on special teams for the Dolphins before he was released and signed this week by the Panthers. Released OLB Cam Gill from the practice squad Gill has been in and out of Carolina going back to 2024. Between 2020 and 2023 he appeared in 40 games for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with 29 tackles and 2.5 sacks. In 2024 he came to Carolina and played in 10 games for the Panthers, registering a solid 22 tackles. That year he played 221 defensive snaps for the Panthers and 172 on special teams. He didn’t play in the NFL last year and has bounced around Carolina’s practice squad in 2026 without yet taking the field. Released DT Anthony Goodlow from the practice squad Goodlow was originally signed to the Panthers practice squad on September 1, 2026 and had managed to survive up to this point without getting waived then re-signed. But, here we are. The 26-year-old undrafted player spent most of 2024 on the Cardinals practice squad without playing in a game. Last year he had three tackles in three games for Arizona before coming to Carolina this year. He’s now once again on the move.

stories.title: Eagles place Will Shipley on injured reserve
stories.summary: Two of Philadelphia’s top three running backs have landed on IR.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Will Shipley #28 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up before a game against the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are placing Will Shipley on injured reserve, according to an official team announcement. Shipley, who started on Sunday, reportedly suffered “ a partial tear of his plantar fascia ” during the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. By going on IR, Shipley will automatically miss the Eagles’ next four games: Week 6 vs. Carolina Panthers Week 7 vs. Dallas Cowboys Week 8 at Washington Commanders Week 9 vs. New York Giants The Eagles then have their bye in Week 10 so the earliest we could see Shipley back is Week 11, when they host the Pittsburgh Steelers. With Saquon Barkley still nursing a hamstring injury and Tank Bigsby also on IR, the Eagles are currently without their top three running backs. Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele are the only healthy backfield options on the roster. The team also has Jaydon Blue and newly signed Ian Wheeler on the practice squad. Putting Shipley on IR frees up a roster spot for the Eagles signing Joe Milton III away from the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad .

stories.title: NFL removes Broncos OLB Jonathon Cooper from Commissioner's Exempt List
stories.summary: The NFL has announced it has removed Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner's Exempt List.
stories.detailText: The NFL has announced it has removed Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner's Exempt List. Cooper is eligible to play in the team's next game on Oct. 25 after missing six games. The NFL placed Cooper on paid leave on Aug. 30 following domestic-related charges involving two incidents with his former girlfriend in June. Cooper's motion hearing was continued on Monday at the request of the district attorney’s office. He is now scheduled for a motion hearing on Feb. 23 and a jury trial the week of March 2. The NFL season ends with Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 14. Cooper is facing five charges after two disputes with his ex-girlfriend that began with a fight over a cell phone. The most serious charge is felony second-degree assault/strangulation. He participated in the team's training camp and three preseason games after pleading not guilty to all charges. Cooper lost $180,000 in per-game roster bonuses but was able to keep his six weekly game checks of $676,471 each while on leave. In its statement, the league said it will continue to investigate and monitor Cooper's legal matter until a resolution.

stories.title: Jalen Hurts' health bigger than football, as teammates, coach detail QB concern
stories.summary: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni declined to offer much detail about Jalen Hurts' health, instead focusing on his connection with the quarterback.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- Eagles coach Nick Sirianni declined to offer much detail about Jalen Hurts ' health Friday, instead focusing on his connection with the quarterback. "I'm always concerned for our guys. Jalen and I have a special relationship. There's times I've said to Jalen, 'I know you like I know my brother,'" Sirianni said at a news conference. "We've spent a lot of time together. We've been to the highest of highs, we've had lows. ... Your first reaction is always the care for the player because this is not just a coach-player relationship." Hurts has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers due to a superficial blood clot in his calf. The Eagles released a lengthy statement Thursday detailing the process that led to the discovery of the blood clot. The quarterback was cleated Week 4 against the Los Angeles Rams and requested treatment on the calf the following Thursday, according to the team. An ultrasound on Saturday in London revealed the blood clot, though Hurts played in Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars after the Eagles' medical staff and doctors "reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play." A follow-up ultrasound Wednesday night "revealed movement in the small blood clot," leading to the decision to sit Hurts against the Panthers. The Eagles have not provided a timeline for his return. "I know there's a great deal of interest in Jalen's health, but I'm not going to get too much into any of that," Sirianni said when asked if a course of treatment has been established for Hurts. "Jalen's health is the utmost important to all of us in this building, care deeply about Jalen." Most Eagles players found out about Hurts' health situation as they took the field for Thursday's walk-through. "It's hard when you find out your leader has to sit out for something like that," wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks said. "It's real serious. You never know what people are going through because he played the game last week and we didn't know. But we just stick by his side and be there for him while he's going through what he's going through and just doing what we've got to do until he gets back." Tanner McKee will get the start in Hurts' absence. Several skill position players expressed confidence in McKee, a 2023 sixth-round pick out of Stanford , as they navigate the loss of their QB1 for an unknown amount of time. "He's fine," said wide receiver DeVonta Smith , when asked if he has had a chance to talk with Hurts. "It's bigger than football. Something like this that's very serious puts a lot of things into perspective."

stories.title: 'Enough already.' Former Bronco defends QB Bo Nix after scathing criticism
stories.summary: Former NFL QB Ryan Fitzpatrick said Bo Nix's play was "almost disrespectful to the quarterback position" on the Thursday Night Football postgame show.
stories.detailText: A former Denver Broncos player is coming to Bo Nix's defense. The Brocos quarterback has been widely criticized after his Oct. 15 performance in a 17-14 overtime win over the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks on "Thursday Night Football," including a scathing take from former NFL quarterback and current Prime Video analyst Ryan Fitzpatrick on the postgame show. "It was really frustrating to watch," Fitzpatrick said. "Bo Nix is not playing competitively, it's almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he's playing football." Ed McCaffrey, who played for the Broncos from 1995 to 2003 and won three Super Bowls during his NFL career, took to social media on Friday to defend Nix. "Stop, just stop," McCaffrey wrote of the Nix criticism on X. "Enough already. Apparently winning isn't enough anymore." Stop, just stop. Enough already. Apparently winning isn’t enough anymore. Bo Nix and the @Broncos weren’t perfect but they still won the game. Winning in the NFL is hard. Enjoy it. #BroncosCountry — Ed McCaffrey (@87ed) October 16, 2026 Nix, in his sixth game back after fracturing his ankle in a January playoff game, completed 17 of 27 passes for 107 yards and ran four times for 2 yards in the win over the Seahawks on Thursday. The Broncos finished with just 168 total yards. Fitzpatrick went so far as to question Nix's effort and competitiveness after the game and even said Broncos head coach Sean Payton has "no trust" in him. "I can only imagine how Sean Payton feels," Fitzpatrick said. "I mean, Sean Payton, (offensive coordinator) Davis Webb, everybody that blocks for (Nix). He's not competing right now, and that's something that he's hung his hat on for the last two years. I don't know if he's still injured, I don't know what's going on. But it's not good enough. It's effort." McCaffrey objected to that criticism. In reply to a fan who said it was fair to criticize Nix, the former wide receiver and father of superstar 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey said it's "fair game" to "criticize the throws, the decisions, the offense." "But questioning Bo's heart and desire to win? That's a different story," McCaffrey wrote. Absolutely fair. Criticize the throws, the decisions, the offense. All fair game. But questioning Bo’s heart and desire to win? That’s a different story. And since when did celebrating a win become controversial? 😂 We can do both. #BroncosCountry — Ed McCaffrey (@87ed) October 16, 2026 The Broncos are 4-2 this season after facing a daunting start to the schedule that has included wins over the Jaguars, Rams, Chargers and Seahawks along with losses to the undefeated Chiefs and 49ers. "The grass isn't always greener," McCaffrey told another commenter. "And 4-2 ain't bad." Fair point. Bo’s play is absolutely fair game for criticism. But there are teams with Super Bowl-winning and All-Pro QBs wondering the same thing. The grass isn’t always greener. 😂 And 4-2 ain’t bad. — Ed McCaffrey (@87ed) October 16, 2026 This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: 'Enough already.' stories.title: Inside the NFL game management world tasked with preventing snafus like Commanders just had: 'It's irresponsible not to learn from others' mistakes'
stories.summary: Game-management coordinators typically speak more on the gameday headset than their position-coach colleagues. But it's not an exact science, as the Commanders showed.
stories.detailText: In an ideal world, the Washington Commanders would have had The Conversation before their last drive. We have no timeouts. We can't take a sack. We need an out-of-bounds or end-zone play that sets up our kicker at his preferred hash. In this ideal world, the Commanders would have already circulated end-of-game situational awareness through training camp and, to some degree, throughout practice and game-planning during the week. They'd have assessed their time cutoffs during training camp to understand how long several of their plays and operational considerations take, knowing precisely what they need to bleed the clock but still leave time for a spike and field-goal attempt. And after all that had happened, in this ideal world, head coach Dan Quinn would have directed offensive coordinator David Blough before the Commanders' overtime two-minute drive what the team's yardage and play-clock threshold was to set up a field goal for a kicker who had already missed an extra point that day. Before the play that QB Jayden Daniels ultimately snapped with 12 seconds left, Quinn — perhaps aided by his game management staffers — would have reminded Blough the time cutoff for a spike, Blough would have reminded Daniels he can't take a sack and has no timeouts, and Daniels (perhaps running a play-call that didn't involve a personnel substitution and take more time) would have reminded teammates the situation. Daniels and teammates would have kicked into urgency mode to get the last spike off. The Commanders still might have missed the kick. But perhaps they would have avoided the operational fiasco that triggered Quinn slamming his headset, part team owner Magic Johnson tweeting he was "in total disbelief my Commanders had such poor clock management," and Daniels telling his teammates of the missed chance that left the Commanders tied with the New York Giants: "It'll never happen again." The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0 — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 How many of these ideal steps happened? It's near impossible to know. But seeing the play triggered coaches and game-management coordinators around the league who know how much has to go right in those situations — and how colleagues' jobs and legacies are on the line. "There are still paths to victory with basically every decision you make," one game management coordinator told Yahoo Sports. "Everyone wants to point fingers and blame one thing and it's not that simple. … "It is seldom one thing." The Commanders' operational failure spotlighted the role of game management coordinators across the NFL, a group whose jobs help prevent these very snafus from happening. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season But how does the process work? How do NFL teams manage game clocks, communicate on headsets and respond to the unexpected in real time? Yahoo Sports spoke to game management coordinators from six NFL teams as well as two former offensive coordinators to better understand. All except former offensive coordinator Scott Turner spoke on condition of anonymity due to concerns about competitive advantage surrounding their team's strategy. (Turner is not currently with an NFL team.) They also emphasized their goal was not to knock the Commanders or other teams with recent late-game struggles, knowing that their own teams and processes have each failed at one point or another. And yet, "it's irresponsible not to learn from other people's mistakes — and from your own," one game management coordinator said. So teams are discussing where the Commanders fell short and how to prevent a repeat. "The fact that it's been so publicized, I think most of the teams are probably having more conversations about it," another game management coordinator said. "But in my opinion, the really good situational teams have already been having those conversations." What do NFL game-management coordinators do? Determining with certainty how many teams have an official game management coordinator is complicated. Titles vary dramatically from one game-management staffer to the next, some teams not even sharing publicly who runs this proprietary role for them. But a Yahoo Sports analysis of NFL media guides, LinkedIn profiles and conversations with coaches in the league identified 21 teams with a game-management role on their coaching staff and 11 teams who have tabbed a front office member to oversee responsibilities. Roles differ among game-management coordinators but tend to start in the same place: managing timeouts; guiding decisions on when to go for it on fourth downs or 2-point conversion attempts; and establishing thresholds in two-minute play to manipulate the clock. From there, roles at times expand to helping head coaches determine when to accept or reject a penalty, devising and sequencing plays during the final two minutes of the half or game, and teaching players and coaches about situational moments that influenced games across the league the prior week. "We have to be flexible," one game-management coordinator said, "because if you're doing stuff that's not hitting their brains, then it's worthless." Some game-management coordinators present to the team one or more times each week during the season, while others collaborate specifically with the head coach or head coach and coordinators. Gradually, trusted game managers around the league are spending weekday time in the quarterback room given how crucial coach, play-caller and quarterback alignment is in situational, less-repped moments. "Those three people need to be on the same page," a game-management coordinator said. Game-management coordinators typically speak more on the gameday headset than their position-coach colleagues, but how active they are on the headset differs, they say. Excelling in the role often requires a keen understanding of coaches' personalities and temperaments. The Washington Commanders' botched finish to a game against the New York Giants put a spotlight on the elaborate world of NFL game management. (Henry Russell/Yahoo Sports) Game-management staffers assess: Does my play-caller prefer to know the viability of four-down territory after first down or after second? How concisely can I deliver all necessary information when an offensive play-caller is not in conversation with the quarterback and the defensive coordinator not communicating to the "green dot" mic-ed up player? What's the most important information and who needs it? Does my play-caller prefer a constant stream of reminders or primarily quiet to think? Different coaches warrant different game-management styles. "I'd much rather get told to shut up on the headset than to not say something and do something stupid out there," one game-management coordinator said. Added another: "People do freeze up as the clock's ticking down, and there's so many people that have the ability to speak up, but you'll be surprised in those situations how sometimes people defer or they're scared to say something out of turn in a stressful situation. "You'll be surprised how often it's crickets." Some head coaches want game-management coordinators talking on the "main" headset lines for offense and defense (and special teams, if the special teams coordinator wears a headset, which not all do) while other head coaches (often non-play callers) prefer a clean line for their game-management coordinator to relay information directly to the head coach, and the head coach to then relay. Sometimes the goal is to inform a decision; other times, to announce it. Guidance will factor in advance scouting of opponents — how does this opponent defend out-of-bounds plays? Hail Marys? The nuances of weighing odds and influential factors swirl in coaches' heads, but the decision-making goal remains generally the same. "We're totally just in risk management," a game-management coordinator said. Recent Cowboys, Eagles losses a reminder that decision making 'not black and white' Practicing situational periods across training camp and in-season practices is standard for NFL teams. Visit a training camp, and it's rare to see a practice that doesn't include a situational period given how often NFL games come down to the fourth quarter and game-winning drives. But one game management coordinator estimated the math as such: Imagine a team practices its bread-and-butter plays three to five times a week. Given the variety of situational outcomes, a team is more likely to practice a single type of situation once every two to three weeks (with other situations practiced in the interim). "I think most teams hit a two-minute drive every week in practice," the coordinator said. "Now, do they have an end-of-game clock situation that comes up? Maybe, maybe not. Definitely not every week. … "You can only spend so much time for the amount of times it's going to come up in a game. You'd love to rep them all a million times and be perfect at them, but it's not realistic." The Commanders aren't the only team to cough up a recent game in the final seconds. The Dallas Cowboys tied the Baltimore Ravens with 7 seconds to play in Rio de Janeiro in Week 3. Overtime seemed imminent, and Dallas opted to kick a touchback that set up the Ravens at their own 35-yard line. A defensive gamble followed, Lamar Jackson completing a 27-yard pass to Zay Flowers and then calling a timeout with 1 second left. Ravens kicker Tyler Loop kicked a game-winning 56-yard field goal to secure the 34-31 victory. Should the Cowboys have forced a return? "I hurt our chance to win that game," head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters afterward. The Philadelphia Eagles' loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars last Sunday called into question Schottenheimer's statement. Playing in London, the Eagles kicked a go-ahead field goal with 8 seconds to play. They chose to kick the ball in bounds, seemingly needing just one good stop from their kick-return unit to guarantee victory. Jacksonville running back Ameer Abdullah executed a well-devised and well-blocked 53-yard return, leaving 1 second on the clock. Kicker Cam Little — who holds the NFL record for longest made kick, at 68 yards — connected from 57 yards. Jaguars win 19-17. The final sequence for the @Jaguars to get the win in London was truly WILD. pic.twitter.com/5viJ5yIdIX — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 The scenarios weren't completely identical. But they were similar, the Cowboys and Ravens opted for opposite strategies, and each lost. "Having two different outcomes just shows you that it's not black and white," a game-management coordinator said. And while game-planning is crucial, strategy can only take a team so far, former NFL offensive coordinator Scott Turner told Yahoo Sports. "At some point, you still have to tackle people, you still have to cover a kickoff," said Turner, who coordinated the Carolina Panthers, Washington Commanders and Las Vegas Raiders offenses in various stints between 2019-24. "The game management stuff [is] all tools. It's information. But you got to block people and you got to tackle people and you got to catch it and you got to run good routes." The Commanders have their first chance to move forward from their botched end-of-game on Monday, when they face the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers on the road in prime time. The spotlights will be bright. The opponent, by record, more successful. Throughout the weekend, expect not only the Commanders but every NFL team to dial in on how they prepare for situational football and how they communicate that preparation in the heat of the game. Expect play-callers to await the advice, and the communication, streaming through their headsets. "Just that overcommunication, making sure everyone's on the same page," a second former offensive coordinator said. "So when all hell's breaking loose, no one's caught off guard."

stories.detailText: The Seattle Seahawks offense is broken. While the disaster on Thursday night wasn’t all on the team’s offensive line, the Seahawks front certainly didn’t do their quarterback, Sam Darnold, any favors. Well, have no fear, Seahawks fans! Because help is on the way. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said that starting right guard Anthony Bradford has a very good chance to return next Sunday in the team’s showdown with the Kansas City Chiefs. Mike Macdonald said there’s a very good chance injured RG Anthony Bradford will return next Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs — Andrew Destin (@AndrewDestin1) October 16, 2026 A rotation of Christian Haynes and rookie Beau Stephens has replaced Bradford, with both guards being a mixed bag through four weeks. The Seahawks offensive line has struggled significantly in 2026, and Bradford’s return could be a boost, especially for right tackle Abraham Lucas. stories.title: Josh Jacobs will be removed from paid leave on Monday
stories.summary: NFL leaves door open for further discipline.
stories.detailText: The efforts of Packers running back Josh Jacobs to keep the NFL from seeing the video of the altercation that resulted in his no-contest plea for battery has worked. For now. The NFL has announced that Jacobs will be reinstated from the Commissioner Exempt list on Monday. The timing isn't coincidental. With the baseline punishment for domestic battery under the Personal Conduct Policy set at six games, the move allows the league to pre-suspend a player whose internal investigation is still pending. Then, if/when a suspension is imposed, he'll get credit for the games missed while on paid leave — and he'll forfeit the pay he received during the games in which he didn't play. Although paid leave technically isn't discipline (even though, as a practical matter, it is), the missed games become part of the eventual discipline. And the league's decision to reserve the right to add additional games ties directly to the video that it wants to review before it closes his case. It's a risky move for the NFL. Until it sees the video, it won't know whether the video contains images that would justify a much more significant punishment than a six-game suspension. The better play, given Jacobs's efforts to keep the league from seeing the video, would be to tell him that he won't play at all until the league sees the video. If, in the end, the video is as shocking as the Ray Rice video from 2014 was, the NFL will have another P.R. mess on its hands. Maybe, after 12 years, the memory of extent of the Ray Rice situation has faded. Either way, the safest approach would have been to tell Jacobs that, until the video is seen by the league, his stay on paid leave will continue.
